Permissions
  • Guest can discover institution names only.
  • Untrusted return parameters must never become arbitrary external redirects.
  • Roles and enrollment arrive from authoritative records; no self-selected privilege.
Responsive
  • Centered form becomes full-width with readable margins at 320 CSS pixels.
  • Long institution names and hosts wrap; primary button follows the selected result.
Accessibility
  • Search is a labelled combobox with keyboard selection and announced result count.
  • Authentication permits paste and password managers at the institutional service; no cognitive puzzle is added.
Data
  • Institution directory fixture: identifier, display name, trusted host, support URL.
  • Validated internal return context; no credentials in logs or fixtures.
Acceptance checks (3)
  • A deep link to an assignment returns to its access check after W02.
  • Typing an unknown name leaves Continue unavailable with an explicit reason.
  • A failed handoff never renders authenticated navigation or invents a session.
Notes
  • PROPOSED academic web route template for HTML-first handoff; legacy IDs show lineage, not replacement or changed acceptance.
  • IdP, institution and authentication protocol remain partner decisions. HTML uses an explicitly labelled simulated redirect.

Permissions
  • Successful authentication alone grants no course access.
  • A consumed callback cannot create duplicate sessions or invitation acceptance.
  • Staff and learner landing choices use assigned roles only.
Responsive
  • One status card; recovery actions stack on narrow screens.
  • No layout shift from loading to error that hides the recovery heading.
Accessibility
  • Announce verification outcome once; move focus to the outcome heading.
  • Error reference is selectable text; never announce token or internal exception strings.
Data
  • Simulated verification outcome, safe destination, account and role summary.
  • Redacted correlation reference and institution support owner.
Acceptance checks (3)
  • Expired callback opens a fresh W01 flow without a redirect loop.
  • Valid first use goes to W04 and retains the original return.
  • A guessed course URL still receives access checking after identity succeeds.
Notes
  • PROPOSED academic web route template for HTML-first handoff; legacy IDs show lineage, not replacement or changed acceptance.
  • HTML models outcomes; it does not validate real credentials or implement an auth protocol.

Permissions
  • Only matching recipient sees full invitation facts.
  • Course invitation cannot grant institution administration or unrelated course access.
  • TA acceptance grants allocated scope, never policy or release authority.
Responsive
  • Role and expiry facts stack before the primary action.
  • Long recipient addresses wrap; no clipped mismatch warning.
Accessibility
  • Use a definition list for role facts and a visible checkbox label.
  • Acceptance error links focus the checkbox or identity recovery action.
Data
  • Invitation fixture: masked recipient, inviter, course, role, scope, expiry, status.
  • Existing membership status distinguishes invited from active.
Acceptance checks (3)
  • Wrong-account view cannot expose full recipient address or learner records.
  • An expired invitation cannot be accepted after a stale page is left open.
  • Double activation produces one accepted result and one existing-access view.
Notes
  • PROPOSED academic web route template for HTML-first handoff; legacy IDs show lineage, not replacement or changed acceptance.

  • Staff role expiry can remove historical staff access even when student enrollment remains.
Responsive
  • Cards become a single list; filters wrap rather than require horizontal scrolling.
  • Preserve selected year/term after returning from a course.
Accessibility
  • Current/Past are links or buttons with announced selection, not unlabeled decorative tabs.
  • Read-only and unavailable use text alongside icons; course names remain complete.
Data
  • Course membership summary, institution term catalog, retention/access status.
  • Next-work summaries only for authorized current contexts.
Acceptance checks (3)
  • Selecting Fall 2025 cannot reveal another user's retained submissions.
  • Archive course opens read-only and blocks stale submission actions.
  • A term lookup error shows retry rather than 'you have no courses'.
Notes
  • PROPOSED academic web route template for HTML-first handoff; legacy IDs show lineage, not replacement or changed acceptance.

Permissions
  • Only released score/comment/rubric payloads enter this page.
  • Group learner sees own applicable released outcome; individual overrides are private.
  • TA may review request only in scoped staff workflow; learner cannot release or edit grades.
  • Instructor entry is an explicitly labeled, read-only learner preview for an authorized selected course member. It does not impersonate the learner or permit review requests, replies, read-state changes or other learner actions.
Responsive
  • On narrow web, work and matching feedback stack with explicit page/question selector.
  • Criterion detail can open a full-width drawer with reading position retained.
Accessibility
  • Annotations have a textual list keyed to page/question.
  • Score and status have spoken labels; history comparisons do not rely only on red/green.
Data
  • Immutable typed result snapshots: reviewed_attempt links receipt/rubric; status_outcome links assessment/person/policy and no fabricated attempt.
  • Released category explanation and linked correction request status; history selector may use releaseId query without requiring an attempt URL.
Acceptance checks (5)
  • An unreleased staff edit never changes displayed score, rubric or comments.
  • Updated feedback preserves the earlier released payload in history.
  • A failed review request remains unsent and cannot change score or deadline.
  • Clarification failure retains unsent text; success updates the existing W54 request, never posts a discussion reply or changes the released grade.
  • A released Missing/Excused result can open feedback without an attemptId or receipt; no numeric/page content is invented. A policy-only course-total change opens W24 instead.
Notes
  • PROPOSED academic web route template for HTML-first handoff; legacy IDs show lineage, not replacement or changed acceptance.

Permissions
  • Student sees own results only; staff preview uses an explicit sample identity.
  • All learner arithmetic uses released snapshots, including released missing/excused status.
  • No TA policy edit/release actions; SIS remains authoritative for official final grades.
  • Instructor entry is an explicitly labeled, read-only learner preview for an authorized selected course member. It does not impersonate the learner or permit review requests, replies, read-state changes or other learner actions.
Responsive
  • Table becomes labelled rows; category method and result status remain visible.
  • Calculation detail uses vertical arithmetic at narrow widths.
Accessibility
  • Table headers identify earned/possible points and release status.
  • Arithmetic has readable textual equations, not an image-only explanation.
Data
  • Published policy and assessment-category mapping; immutable released result set.
  • Release-only included/excluded items, category methods, exact calculation and rounded display.
  • Use data/fixtures.json primary course policy and independent method-test scenario; calculations specified in spec/04_WORKFLOWS_AND_RECORDS.md.
Acceptance checks (4)
  • Canonical method test: released 10/10 plus 50/100 yields equal 75% and proportional 60/110 = 54.54545...% before final display rounding.
  • Primary PHYS 110 fixture shows learner 84.50%; held PS4 27/30 changes staff to 85.17% while learner remains 84.50%.
  • Missing and excused affect learner totals only after release; an empty category never creates NaN/Infinity.
  • The separate proposed 10/25/25/40 policy-editor scenario reconciles with its own mapped assessments.
Notes
  • PROPOSED academic web route template for HTML-first handoff; legacy IDs show lineage, not replacement or changed acceptance.
  • New complete learner view; legacy S09/S19 are lineage rather than an assertion that the accepted baseline already contained it.

Keep reading rulesStart attempt now
Permissions
  • Learner can start only own eligible attempt.
  • TA cannot alter quiz window, allowance policy or release.
  • Focus/visibility events are never proof of cheating and cannot auto-cancel an attempt.
Responsive
  • Rules precede Start on narrow web; timing summary remains readable.
  • Large tables of rules become definition lists.
Accessibility
  • Timing is explained in text before acknowledgement.
  • No keyboard trap/fullscreen dependency; institution-approved accessibility timing exceptions are surfaced.
Data
  • Published quiz version, personal timing, own attempt status and release rule.
  • Integrity disclosure and allowed tools/materials; no answer keys on rules page.
Acceptance checks (4)
  • Opening or refreshing rules does not consume an attempt.
  • A timed-out start resolves an existing attempt before offering another Start.
  • Course AI prohibition is shown even if W11 lists an eligible AI tool.
  • Starting 9 minutes before personal close warns that the remaining window is 9 minutes even when personal timer duration is 30; start records that earlier effective deadline.
Notes
  • PROPOSED academic web route template for HTML-first handoff; legacy IDs show lineage, not replacement or changed acceptance.
  • Proposed quiz deadline = earlier of personal close and startedAt + effective duration; untimed quiz ends at personal close. Show a shortened window before Start. Use one timer allowance mode (extra minutes OR multiplier), not both. At expiry finalize only acknowledged answers; unsent offline text remains a recoverable local draft requiring staff review, never a fake accepted receipt.

Return to answersSubmit attempt
Permissions
  • Only learner's active attempt is editable; authorization rechecked on resume.
  • Attempt prompts/order/rules remain snapshotted despite later authoring.
  • No client focus counter deletes answers, changes grade or automatically cancels.
Responsive
  • Question navigation becomes a labelled collapsible list on narrow web.
  • Timer/save strip cannot obscure prompt or keyboard-focused answer.
Accessibility
  • Timer uses role=timer without announcing every second; meaningful warnings are polite.
  • Question inputs use fieldsets, labels, units and accessible math/media; all review navigation works by keyboard.
Data
  • Immutable quiz-attempt question/rule snapshot and personal deadline.
  • Per-answer draft/acknowledged versions, review flags and submission operation state.
Acceptance checks (4)
  • Quiz edits after Start never alter this attempt's prompts or answers.
  • A connectivity loss preserves acknowledged answers and labels unsent edits honestly.
  • Repeated submit/status checks resolve one receipt; focus loss never auto-cancels.
  • At effective deadline, lock edits and resolve finalization of acknowledged answers once; offline unacknowledged edits remain labeled unsent and require recovery, not an invented accepted timestamp.
Notes
  • PROPOSED academic web route template for HTML-first handoff; legacy IDs show lineage, not replacement or changed acceptance.
  • Proposed quiz deadline = earlier of personal close and startedAt + effective duration; untimed quiz ends at personal close. Show a shortened window before Start. Use one timer allowance mode (extra minutes OR multiplier), not both. At expiry finalize only acknowledged answers; unsent offline text remains a recoverable local draft requiring staff review, never a fake accepted receipt.

Keep unread stateMark visible read
Permissions
  • Learners never see draft/scheduled announcement titles or counts.
  • TA read access follows course scope; no automatic announcement publishing authority.
  • Announcements are course communication, never a direct-message channel.
Responsive
  • Rows become stacked cards; pin/read state precedes excerpt.

Data
  • Published announcement ID/version, audience visibility, author, timestamps and pin.
  • Personal read marker and accessible list pagination.
Acceptance checks (3)
  • A scheduled announcement does not appear before publication through filters or count.
  • Turning optional delivery off retains published announcements here.
  • Read-marker failure leaves old status visible and offers retry.

Permissions
  • Learner cannot create/delete group sets, move others or change grading policy.

At expiry finalize only acknowledged answers; unsent offline text remains a recoverable local draft requiring staff review, never a fake accepted receipt.

WhenPolicy changed without new marks, or missing/excused outcome awaits publication
ShowsShow exact old/new learner totals or status, exclusions and source versions. Keep receipt blank when no accepted attempt exists.
Way outReview candidate payload and release exact projection/status; retain prior version history.
Dialogs and drawers (1)
Release exact feedback
  • Recipient count, sample learner payload, exceptions, quiz key visibility and snapshot fingerprint
  • Graded does not mean released; delivery outcome is separate
Return without applying changesRelease reviewed snapshot
Permissions
  • Instructor alone prepares and confirms release; TA may see own completion status but cannot open bulk release payloads.
  • Each learner later opens only their own released snapshot, never peers' results or held revisions.
Responsive
  • Use labelled sequential steps; narrow web previews one recipient at a time with selected count and exclusions persistent.
  • Do not hide old/new result differences behind a release button; stale status and final acknowledgment remain next to confirmation.
Accessibility
  • Announce step changes and stale-preview errors; validation returns focus to the changed recipient or acknowledgment.
  • Preview tables name learner, score, receipt and version. Final dialog states recipients/content and restores focus; confirmation cannot depend on colour or a visual checkbox alone.
Data
  • Instructor-only fingerprint binds candidate kind,exact recipients,payload,policy version,actual attempt/receipt and rubric when applicable,and captured membership where relevant.
  • Release snapshots are immutable; operation ID supports uncertain-outcome checks. Notification delivery is separate. TA receives completion status, never bulk release payloads.
  • Discriminated release candidate: reviewed_attempt, status_outcome or policy_projection. Receipt required only for reviewed_attempt; policy projection binds only released item/status snapshots and policy version.
Acceptance checks (6)
  • A comment edit after preview blocks release even if scores did not change.
  • Group receipt produces member-specific result snapshots with common work and explicit overrides.
  • Release failure/uncertain outcome offers status check by operation ID and never creates duplicate snapshots on retry.
  • Publish a new policy-only course-total projection without a new score or receipt; stale score/policy changes invalidate its preview.
  • Release Missing/Excused outcomes without a fabricated submission or completed numeric review; student W24 sees the approved status/denominator only after release.
  • A course-wide policy release navigates without an assessmentId; Nothing ready appears only when all three candidate kinds are ineligible.
Notes
  • NEW PROPOSED web template; legacy IDs/map unchanged.
  • HTML planning only; no backend/integrations.
Sources
design/batch03/screens_grade.jsdesign/decisions.mdST05

  • Export is a local content download, with no claim of live SIS grade delivery or third-party compatibility.
Notes
  • NEW PROPOSED web template; legacy IDs/map unchanged.
  • HTML planning only; no backend/integrations.

Document 03 · Spec 01 · Product and scope

From spec/01_PRODUCT_AND_SCOPE.md

Product, scope and vocabulary

Whiteboard helps a student find academic work, complete it, know it was received and understand released feedback. It helps an instructor organize a course, assess work and publish trustworthy results. It helps a TA complete explicitly assigned teaching/grading work without inheriting the instructor's authority.

Academic web scope

Include institution sign-in handoff and arrival, role/course context, courses and archives, syllabus/modules/materials, assignments and group assignments, supported quizzes, submissions and receipts, rubrics/grading/release, learner course grades, configurable grading policy, announcements/discussions, academic calendars/private planning, TA allocation/deadlines, tools access, account/search/help, scoped attendance/insights and course copy/content import/export.

The new package expands incomplete academic workflows identified in the coworker review. It contains a proposed full design inventory, not a first-school deployment commitment. Files can become components, subroutes or page variants later, but a layout consolidation must preserve every listed task and state. Renaming a page does not justify dropping its fields, privacy or recovery rules.

Exclude campus life/organizations, event booking, registrar timetable optimization, advising/case work, financial/clinical/official SIS records, university administration, a direct-message inbox, live video conferencing, native iOS/Android and autonomous final grading. An academic calendar may display institution-owned class meetings as a read-only source; it does not grant a professor permission to edit registrar records. Existing broader designs remain untouched.

Achievements and a course FAQ assistant have optional specifications so the ideas are not lost. Do not implement them in the first required academic build. Secure-browser/proctoring support is discovery only. Tab/window state cannot prove cheating, and no automatic attempt cancellation is proposed.

Product language

TermExact meaning
Course offeringOne course in one institution/term/section context, not the reusable catalog title.
EnrollmentA person's course-scoped role and access window. One person may hold different roles in different courses.
ModuleOrdered course unit with publication, availability and prerequisite rules.
AssessmentAssignment or quiz with a stable ID, published instructions, dates, allowed attempts and grading policy mapping.
Due date / close dateDue marks expected completion; close stops ordinary new submissions. Allowances can change personal dates.
Grading deadlineA staff work target; it is independent of student due/close dates.
DraftEditable local/sample work that has not been received.
ReceivedA specific attempt accepted into the sample course record with receipt and versioned contents.
GradedReview is complete in staff scope. It is not necessarily visible to the learner.
ReleasedA specific approved score/comment/rubric snapshot is visible to its learner recipients.
MissingNo accepted work after close under the course's rule; distinguish from ungraded, excused and an interrupted upload.
ExcusedThe assessment is removed from the applicable denominator. It is not zero.
Group set / groupA named cohort partition for a task, and its named member subset. Course sections and TA grading allocations are separate concepts.
ActivityNotices about an underlying academic record; reading/dismissing a notice does not change that record.
ToolA course/institution-approved external resource, with access requirements. A link does not create a software license.
Proposed defaultA concrete starting decision for the first HTML; still revisable by the owner/institution.

Use “Instructor” in UI, with professor understood as the same role here. Use “Teaching assistant” on permission-sensitive screens. Use learner only in staff explanations where useful; “Your grades” suits student navigation.

Content and assessment bounds

First HTML uses rich text with headings, lists, links, images/alternatives, math text, attachments and video placeholders with captions/transcripts. Do not promise collaborative document editing. File requirements are configurable sample data; fixture limits are not permanent product limits.

Quiz design focuses on single-choice, multiple-select, numeric and written-response items. Imported unsupported types must become visible exceptions, not silently altered questions. Essay/file upload through assignments remains a separate path. High-stakes exam lockdown, adaptive tests, plagiarism verdicts and automatic grading of arbitrary handwriting are not implied.

Meeting links may open a plainly labeled external institution tool. The web app does not create a meeting service. Office hours can be recurring course calendar events; appointment booking is a later scoped decision, not an accidental promise.

Evidence and product status

The previous 100 designs were accepted as designs. New proposals here have not received that same acceptance. Public competitor documentation verifies that particular workflows exist, not that every school needs them or that Whiteboard is easier. Validate with the owner and a real institutional partner before setting production scope, retention, assessment rules, integrations, AI processing or operating promises.

Document 04 · Spec 02 · Navigation and permissions

From spec/02_NAVIGATION_AND_PERMISSIONS.md

Navigation and permissions

Every page keeps institution, active course/term and current role clear. Academic content must retain its context when opened from search, calendar or activity. Page IDs are stable planning keys; URL patterns are proposed implementation guidance.

Shells

Access shell (W01-W04): Whiteboard identity, institution chooser/identity handoff, status/recovery and help. No signed-in course navigation before a valid sample identity/context exists. The institution owns credentials; Whiteboard does not draw a fake institutional password box.

Global shell (W05-W12): Today, Courses, Calendar, Activity and Tools in the primary sidebar. Top bar contains search, account, active role/context and help. Student home leads with next academic work; instructor home leads with course preparation/grading/release exceptions; TA home leads with assigned work and its deadline. Course roles come from enrollments, not an unrestricted production role switch.

Student course shell (W14-W34): Course breadcrumb and term, Overview, Modules, Coursework, Calendar, Announcements, Discussions, Grades and Groups. Syllabus is a visible overview link. Tools can be reached with a course filter. Assignment feedback and receipts remain nested under their assessment. Group access appears only where enrolled; no private course messaging tab.

Staff course shell (W35-W60): Course breadcrumb and term, Builder, Assessments, Grading, Gradebook, People, Groups, Calendar, Announcements, Discussions and Settings. Files, Rubrics, Question bank, Allowances, Grading allocations, Insights and Copy/Import appear as grouped course tools rather than an unstructured 26-item sidebar. A TA sees only allowed entries and informative read-only views. A deep URL still requires a permission check.

System template (W13): Distinct session-expired, access-denied, not-found, maintenance and service-error variants with safe navigation. Hide private record metadata on unauthorized pages. A 404 response must not confirm that another student's submission exists.

Optional achievements/assistant entries are absent by default. If enabled later, keep their dependency and course-policy rules explicit. No admin/campus navigation should appear just because the historical prototype includes it.

Role and action matrix

CapabilityStudentInstructorTA
Published course contentOwn enrolled coursesOwn managed courses; explicit student previewAssigned courses within access window
View learner gradesOwn released results onlyAuthorized course roster; staff drafts and releases distinguishedAssigned grading scope; no unrelated learner data
Submit individual workOwn attemptsSeparate attributed submit-on-behalf flow only if later selectedNo impersonated submission
Submit group workCurrent authorized member; submission snapshots recipientsReview/correct through explicit workflowAssigned review only
Author/publish assessments and materialsNoYesRead/reference; editing only if later separately granted, off by default
GradeNoCourse scopeAssigned assessments/learners/questions only
Resolve score-affecting conflictRequest correctionYes, with historyFlag for instructor; cannot overwrite competing review
Release/re-release resultsNoYesNo
Change grading policy/weightsNoYes, current impact previewNo
Apply score-affecting rubric rule changeNoYes, explicit impact reviewPropose only
Record allowances / excuse workRequest through typed contextYes; documentation stays in designated officeView adjusted timing when needed; no basis reference; cannot grant
Manage course rolesNoWithin institution-allowed course rolesNo; never self-escalate
Set group membership / work audienceJoin only when self-enrollment enabledYes, with in-progress/received impact checksRead; editing off by default
Announce to classReadDraft/publish/scheduleNo publish by default
DiscussionsPost/read within audience/windowConfigure/moderateParticipate; moderation only if explicitly granted
Private calendarOwn onlyOwn only; no student private eventsOwn only; no student private events
Course meeting editsNoWhiteboard-owned events onlyNo by default
Assign grading tasks/deadlinesNoYesView own, report progress; cannot allocate to self
AttendanceOwn permitted facts/correction requestCourse records and correctionsAssigned sessions only if granted
Copy/import/exportOwn permitted download onlyAuthorized course content; no automatic student record exportNo bulk course export

This is a proposed default matrix for HTML review. Real authorization must later be enforced server-side; disabled buttons, hidden menus and client-side role switches do not secure production data.

Navigation rules

  • Global links retain the selected term/filter. Course links preserve courseId; assessment links preserve assignment/quiz and attempt IDs. Browser Back returns to the previous list/query/date and scroll position when feasible.
  • Course switcher lists only accessible offerings. If an equivalent destination exists in another course, navigate there; otherwise use that course's overview and announce the context change. Never carry a learner/attempt ID into an unrelated course.
  • On role change, clear sensitive rendered data and reload permitted records. Expired TA access blocks mutation immediately and offers an instructor contact/recovery path; saved attributed grading remains intact.
  • Student preview is conspicuous and reversible. It uses the publication/availability rules of a real student and cannot submit, mark completion, trigger reminders or release results.
  • Unsaved work prompts Save draft / Discard / Keep editing where saving is supported. An unavailable network cannot produce “Saved to course.” Maintain the distinction between local draft, queued work and accepted record.
  • Direct links into archived courses show read-only context and current access conditions. Membership/retention checks apply even if the user remembers an old URL.
  • Use ordinary links for navigation. Preserve modified clicks, copy-link and browser history. Use buttons for actions. Sort/filter controls retain query state; state-demo controls remain outside product UI.
  • Calendar source colors supplement text. Private events, course events, student due dates and staff grading targets are separately toggleable sources. Hiding a source never changes its records.

Counting and legacy mapping

The new W inventory deliberately makes previously omitted academic workflows explicit. W24 is a real learner course gradebook; W52 is policy configuration; W47 is group management; W57 supplies TA grading deadlines. They are not satisfied by a generic menu label or a historical S19 staff table. data/legacy-crosswalk.json maps every included S/P academic destination to this proposal. Historical IDs and original accepted tracker remain unchanged.

Document 05 · Spec 03 · Shared UI and states

From spec/03_SHARED_UI_AND_STATES.md

Shared UI, states and design direction

Page-level specifications inherit this contract. Apply only the states relevant to the task; use an explicit N/A rationale instead of decorative empty/error screens. All new interaction details are proposed defaults for the first HTML.

Visual direction

Preserve Whiteboard teal, neutral surfaces, system typography, restrained hierarchy and realistic academic content. The original source tokens are in resources/design-system/. Historical comments saying “proposal/not accepted” are preserved provenance; the owner later accepted the original visual direction. New page layouts still need review.

Light palette: page #f3f4f5, surface #ffffff, ink #16191b, secondary ink #575e63, identity teal #007176, focus blue #0a66d8. Dark palette: page #0f1112, surface #1b1e20, ink #eef1f2, teal #5cc8c8. Do not use the dark fill color as label text on a light background without checking the relevant pair.

Use system sans-serif with a compact but readable hierarchy: proposed web body 16px, secondary 14px, page title 28-32px, section title 18-20px, 1.45-1.6 body line-height. Older references use a 15px web body; the proposed 16px is an intentional new starting default. Prefer 4px spacing increments. Keep primary forms around 640-760px, reading text around 65-80 characters per line, and allow staff work tables to use the available desktop width.

Coursework lists should look like readable work lists; grades should be a structured table; calendars should have a visible agenda alternative; grading should prioritize evidence and score entry. Avoid styling every page as a grid of identical dashboard cards. Use actual course names, dates and specimen work, not marketing text or arbitrary metrics. No remote fonts, decorative stock images or icon library dependencies are needed. The initial mark can be typographic Whiteboard; a new brand logo is not required.

The frontend developer may improve spacing, typography and visual treatment while preserving semantics, contrast, task hierarchy and workflow rules. Keep tokens separate from content and behavior. Do not redraw the existing iPhone frames for this web-only task.

Layout and responsive behavior

  • Desktop: persistent sidebar, compact top bar, task-specific canvas. 1280-1440px is a useful design starting width, not a fixed requirement. Grading may use roster/evidence/score panes when space allows.
  • Intermediate width: collapse secondary rails into sections or drawers with the same headings and context. Do not silently remove learner identity, score maxima, due dates or save status.
  • Narrow web: around 320-768 CSS pixels, use a navigation disclosure and stacked content. Keep primary actions reachable and labeled. This is responsive web, not a native tab-bar promise.
  • Gradebook/data matrices may scroll within a labeled region while the surrounding page reflows. Preserve column headers/row identity. Provide a focused single-learner view on narrow screens. Staff bulk editing remains best on desktop, with an explicit usable narrow alternative for review/protective actions.
  • Keyboard, sticky actions and zoom must not cover the focused field or error. Avoid horizontal page scrolling for ordinary text/forms. Render long course titles, filenames, equations, translated-length labels and large grades without clipping.
  • Light/dark preference follows system or explicit setting. Respect reduced motion. Motion answers the user's action; no continuous decorative motion is needed.

Reusable components

ComponentRequired anatomy and behavior
Course context headerCode/title, term/section, current role, publication/read-only indicator, breadcrumb and relevant next action.
Assessment rowTitle, kind, personal due date/time zone, submission/grade status, relevant score only when authorized, one clear primary link.
Status badgeIcon plus words; color is secondary. Held feedback is neutral. Never make “Queued” visually equivalent to “Received.”
FieldPersistent label, required/optional meaning, helper text, current value and associated inline error. Do not use placeholder as label.
Validation summaryOne top summary with links to invalid fields; preserve values. Explain the fix. Errors block the consequential action; warnings require a deliberate review when appropriate.
TableCaption, headers and row identity; proper semantic table by default. Sort buttons announce current direction. Do not add role=grid unless implementing its full keyboard model.
Dialog/drawerNamed title, concise effect, clear confirm/cancel, focus enters and returns logically. Modal content makes background inert; close affordance and Escape behavior are explicit.
Upload queueFilename/type/size, progress per file, processing/error status, retry/remove, alternative input and accessible equivalent. Drag/drop is optional enhancement.
Evidence viewerPage/file list, selected page/question, zoom/rotation and full text alternative; drawing annotation is optional for first HTML, typed comments are required.
Date/time controlExplicit zone and local interpretation, start/end validation, all-day option, recurrence exceptions and personal/course authority. Do not rely only on a dense visual calendar picker.
Draft/save indicatorLast sample save time, dirty/saving/saved locally/failed/conflict states. Saves never imply final submission or publication.
Release previewExact learner/attempt/score/comment/rubric payload, exclusions and version fingerprint. Relevant changes invalidate it.
Activity itemHuman-readable event, source/course, time, unread state, safe destination. Never expose a grade in notification preview.
Tool access cardVerified product/course purpose, eligibility, institutional account requirement, access instructions, owner/support, expiry and external-site label.
Scenario toolbarSeparate prototype chrome for role, record state, failure injection and reset. Never mix these controls into the product's permission model.

State vocabulary and recovery

StateRequired presentation and next action
LoadingStable content skeleton/status for the affected region; do not show fabricated grades or “0” while data is unknown.
First-use emptyExplain what is absent and who can create it. A student cannot receive an instructor-only Create button.
Filtered emptyName active filters; offer Clear filters. Distinguish from having no course data.
InvalidShow exact field error and summary, keep entered values, focus the right field and block only the invalid action.
Saving / local saveShow where the data currently exists. A local draft is not a server acknowledgment.
Save failedRetain draft, describe what was not saved, retry safely or copy permitted text. Never offer false success.
Conflict/staleIdentify the newer version and affected record. Offer compare/reload/keep local draft where safe. Never silently overwrite marks or receipts.
OfflineLabel cached/last-known information. Block final send/release where acknowledgment is required; preserve eligible draft work and explain resume.
Permission unavailableState course/role boundary without leaking other people's private data. Provide safe return/help; mutation remains blocked on direct entry.
Session expiring/expiredWarn without losing work; institutional sign-in return restores an allowed destination and verifies latest state before retry.
Not yet availableName date/prerequisite if the learner is allowed to know it; do not expose hidden answers/material.
ArchivedShow term and read-only policy. Keep allowed historical feedback and receipts; do not invent permanent retention.
SuccessName the actual sample change and next destination. Submissions need receipt; releases need recipient/version history; scheduling needs publication state.
Partial bulk successShow item-level successes/failures; retry failed items only. No “All done” toast while rows remain unresolved.
Denied device permissionOffer file/manual/keyboard alternative. Do not repeatedly request permission or imply user refusal is a course failure.
Destructive actionName scope/count/record and whether reversible. Preserve history where required; Cancel returns without change.

Copy examples: “Upload interrupted. Your 3 selected pages are still in this draft. Retry upload.” “Preview changed. Review the new scores before releasing.” “You can grade assigned questions until Oct 18, 11:59 pm ET. Only the instructor can restore access.” Avoid generic “Something went wrong” without a recovery.

Dates, counters and notification behavior

Store timestamps with an unambiguous zone/offset in fixtures. Display institution zone and personal adjustments clearly; use local dates for all-day items. Due/close and quiz timer settings are separate. Grading deadlines must not change student due dates. A delayed external class schedule should show its last-known timestamp; coursework owned by Whiteboard should not inherit that source's delay label.

Reminders reference an event/version, so moving or cancelling a class invalidates pending reminders. Notification preference changes affect future delivery, not the underlying course record. In HTML, simulate permission granted/denied and delivery pending/failed; no real email/push is required. A read activity item remains traceable to its source. Personal planning data is private even if the user has a staff role in the course.

Accessibility contract

Target WCAG 2.2 AA as a design/implementation goal. This is not a conformance claim or a statement of the institution's legal obligations. Use semantic landmarks/headings, visible labels, keyboard operation, focus visibility, names for icon controls and programmatic status/error associations. Aim for 44px touch controls as a design choice; WCAG 2.2's minimum target rule has different sizing/spacing exceptions. [M01](../research/core-evidence.md), [M09](../research/core-evidence.md).

Use named dialogs with deliberate focus management, a full keyboard alternative to dragging/reordering, and concise error notifications. A plain semantic grade table is preferable to an incomplete spreadsheet keyboard model. [M02-M04](../research/core-evidence.md).

Check 200% text enlargement and reflow at 320 CSS pixels, with contained two-dimensional tables where genuinely needed. Test screen-reader task completion rather than inferring it from ARIA attributes. [M05](../research/core-evidence.md).

Provide text equivalents for handwritten/PDF specimens, captions/transcripts for teaching media and understandable typed math. Keep timers perceivable without announcing every second; allowance and timed-assessment exception behavior needs institutional review. Never disable copy/paste in authentication or force memory puzzles in the prototype. [M10](../research/core-evidence.md).

Detailed component behavior above is the team's proposed contract informed by the linked guidance. Run actual keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, contrast, forced-color and viewport review before claiming acceptance.

Document 06 · Spec 04 · Workflows and records

From spec/04_WORKFLOWS_AND_RECORDS.md

Connected workflows and record contracts

The HTML prototype must keep one consistent fictional record across views. Scenario switches may construct alternate worlds, but clicking through a normal journey must not unexpectedly substitute a different learner, course, deadline or attempt. The records below describe frontend/domain contracts, not a prescribed backend schema.

Record inventory

RecordMinimum meaningful fields
Person / course enrollmentStable person ID, display name, institutional email, course offering ID, role, active window, permitted actions and assigned grading scope.
Course offeringCode/title, institution/term/section, zone, instructors, publish/access/archive state, syllabus/policy version, modules, tool access references.
Module / materialStable ID, order, title, type, body/asset version, publication, releaseAt, prerequisite, accessible alternative; per-learner completion is separate.
AssessmentStable ID, type, title/instructions version, points, category, published audience, due/close, allowed formats/size, attempts, rubric version, AI policy and group set if used.
Quiz / attemptIndependent quiz close/due, time limit, allowance, attempt rule, immutable item/settings snapshot, answers by item ID, save acknowledgment and submit receipt.
Submission / receiptCourse/assessment/learner or group ID, attempt, submitted version, ordered files/pages/tags, actor, accepted time, receipt reference and membership snapshot.
Score/reviewAssessment/attempt/person/question IDs, rubric/manual source, current draft score, comments, reviewed question IDs, reviewer and revision/conflict history.
Release snapshotApproved exact recipients and candidate kind; actual attempt/receipt and rubric when applicable, score/comments or status, policy version, author/time, exclusions, fingerprint and prior release IDs.
Grading policyVersion, points/weighted mode, categories and item membership, within-category method, weights, empty/ungraded/missing/excused rules, rounding and letter boundaries.
Group set / membershipPurpose/course, group IDs, names, members, assigned assessment IDs, self-enrollment rules/window, membership versions and change history.
AllowancePerson/course/assessment, adjusted due/close/timer/attempt rule, author/time, minimal private basis reference restricted to instructor. No medical attachment.
Calendar itemID/source owner, visibility, course/person, start/end/zone or all-day dates, recurrence ID/exception, publication/version, reminder preference reference.
Grading taskAssigned TA/assessment/learner/question scope, target deadline, allocated/remaining work, progress and access window.
Announcement / discussionCourse/audience, author, draft/published/scheduled status, content version, attachments, post/edit times, moderation reasons and reply availability.
ActivitySource record/version, safe title, audience, unread state, event time and destination. Keep visible feed separate from email/push delivery.
Tool / technical requestVerified access/eligibility/help metadata; request ID, user-provided description, explicitly selected diagnostics and attachment status.
Copy/import previewSource/destination content, mapping, excluded learner records, warnings/blockers, changes/fingerprint, owner review and applied result.

In the prototype, IDs/version checks may be ordinary JS state. Future services must enforce them with real authorization, concurrency, storage and audit. Do not design the UI around unsafe assumptions that all clients can read the complete course data.

Critical journeys

  1. Arrival: W01 institution handoff, W02 return/recovery, W03 invitation when present, W04 role/context onboarding, W05 home. Wrong institution/account never activates an invitation; repeated valid acceptance does not duplicate access.
  2. Individual work: W06/W14 course, W16/W17 material, W18/W19 assignment, W20 add work, W21 review, W22 received receipt. Closing an upload or scanning a page does not submit. Final send needs a clear acknowledgment; interrupted/queued remains unreceived.
  3. Grade and release: W48 queue, W49 assigned evidence/questions, W50 impact when needed, W51 staff calculation, W53 exact release, W23/W24 learner results. Saving scores does not certify complete review. A stale preview blocks release. TAs cannot release even through a deep link.
  4. Course setup: W35 builder, W36 syllabus/settings, W37 module, W38 lesson/W39 assets, W40 assignment/W41 quiz and W43/W44 rubric, then publication and student preview W14. Publish validates relevant dates, points, audiences and accessible alternatives.
  5. Quiz: W25 rules, W26 start/save/recovery, W27 receipt, then results according to captured release policy. Author edits after submission cannot change captured question text/options/answers/settings. A fresh authorized attempt uses current settings without destroying prior attempts.
  6. Policy/grades: W52 configure and preview, W51 staff view, W24 released learner view, W54 corrections where needed. Every displayed total must state what is included and which policy/release is used.
  7. Group work: W47 groups, W40 assignment targeting, W33/W34 membership/workspace, W19-W22 shared attempt, W49 grade with group/individual effects, W53 release, W24 individual visibility. A member submits on behalf of a known group; others see the same received version and actor. Post-submission membership changes do not silently redistribute old work/grades.
  8. TA workload: W45 role/scope, W57 allocation/deadline, W05 TA home/W07 calendar, W48 queue, W49 review. Ended access changes actions immediately; original attributed scores stay. Progress is derived from actual assigned review, not page visits.
  9. Communication: W55 draft/schedule/publish, W28/W29 read, W08 notice, W30/W31 discussion and W56 moderation. Drafts never notify students. A hidden post retains author/staff history with role-safe explanations.
  10. Calendar: W32 course events and office hours, W07 combined view/private planning, W08 reminders/preferences. Published events share one ID across views; moving a course event invalidates its earlier reminder. Read-only source meetings cannot be edited as private events.
  11. Exceptions: W46 applies a scoped allowance, W19/W25 show personal rules, W58 attendance correction preserves original evidence, W54 reviews a grade concern without private messaging. Keep student-visible explanation separate from restricted basis/reference.
  12. Term continuity: W06 archive, W59 copy and W60 content import/export. New offering is draft and distinct from original; people, submissions, grades, private discussions, allowances and attendance are not copied as course content.

data/journeys.json lists these as page-ID sequences for implementation tracking. Optional features must not be required to complete them.

Grade calculations and release visibility

Proposed first implementation supports points and category-weighted modes. Advanced custom formulas remain a later decision. Within a weighted category, use proportional points by default; if the instructor selects equal assessment weighting, average each assessment's percentage instead. Do not confuse the two methods.

Weights must total 100% before a weighted policy can be published. Validate finite non-negative values and a named category for every included item; prevent duplicated contribution. An exempt item is removed from numerator and denominator. Received-but-ungraded work is excluded. A course-defined missing item can count zero after close, but learner visibility still follows release. Zero possible points must not cause division by zero. Extra credit needs an explicit rule; leave disabled by default in the first HTML until selected.

For empty categories, proposed default is to redistribute active-category weights proportionally and display “Current grade based on released work”; if all categories are empty, display “No released grade yet.” Also show planned total weight represented so students do not mistake a running grade for a final grade. Test one empty category and all-empty categories with an explicit denominator in each example. The institution can choose a different policy before production.

Round display only at the final step, proposed two decimal places; do not round intermediate category values. Letter ranges must be non-overlapping and cover the selected scale. A policy change after publication needs old/new previews and a new version. It must not silently rewrite already-released feedback snapshots or official records. Whether a new course total itself needs explicit publication is a policy decision: first HTML retains a released learner projection until the instructor confirms the new policy/result projection.

Fixture check: under the accepted example category mix Assignments 40%, Labs 25%, Quizzes 35%, Aisha's released assignment marks 24/30 and 27/30 give 85%; an excused 30-point item is excluded; labs 18/20 give 90%; quiz 8/10 gives 80%. Released course grade = 84.50%. A held PS4 score 27/30 makes the staff calculation 85.1666...%, displayed 85.17%, while the learner remains at 84.50%. Only releasing the new result/projection changes the learner total. data/fixtures.json includes these golden values and a separate configurable 10/25/25/40 example.

Submission and group invariants

  • Received attempts are immutable. A new attempt starts from a copied draft with a new ID/attempt number; old receipt/files/comments remain inspectable under the right permissions.
  • Review includes page order, orientation, question coverage and file readability. Unsupported/corrupt/oversized examples fail with file-specific recovery. Do not claim OCR accuracy or actual malware scanning in HTML.
  • Group receipt names the group, submitting actor, version and recipient membership at acceptance. Duplicate concurrent send reuses the accepted result or asks to refresh; never manufactures two successful attempts from one action.
  • Changing membership while a draft exists warns about access and ownership. Once received, old membership/recipients remain historical. Late join/withdrawal/individual overrides need an explicit instructor decision and audit trail; no automatic retroactive distribution.
  • Grade correction creates a draft revision with old/new comparison and a reason. Earlier releases remain available; learner feedback changes only when a new version is released. Do not rescore manually overridden answers through a bulk rubric rule.

Quiz, copy and integration limits

Quiz save timestamps describe acknowledged state. Proposed timing default: the effective deadline is the earlier of personal close and startedAt plus the effective timer duration; an untimed quiz still ends at personal close. An allowance uses either extra minutes or a multiplier, never both implicitly. Show the available duration before Start if close truncates the timer. At expiry, finalize acknowledged answers once; keep unacknowledged offline edits as an explicitly unsent local draft for recovery/staff review. A frontend cannot guarantee acceptance past the authoritative close or manufacture an accepted timestamp. Specify resume/time-expiry/conflict screens and validate high-stakes adjudication with the institution before production. Never reset time by refreshing, infer cheating from blur, or erase work because a window changed.

Fixtures include separate before-close assignment/group scenarios and a late-start quiz scenario. The default Oct 20 world already contains received PS4 work; do not use it unchanged to demonstrate a fresh first submission. Apply both the scenario clock and named record resets, then complete the normal workflow.

Copy/import runs against an exact current preview. Changing source file, mapping, selected assets or target dates invalidates acceptance. Unsupported question/tool/media types remain visible blockers or acknowledged placeholders. Export/download is a local fictional sample in HTML; it does not send official grades to an SIS. LTI services and content formats require selected versions and real integration work later. [M06](../research/core-evidence.md).

Document 07 · Spec 05 · Build and acceptance

From spec/05_BUILD_AND_ACCEPTANCE.md

HTML-first build and acceptance

Build a coherent academic prototype in stages, with source files the frontend developer can restyle. The first deliverable is HTML design, not a complete production frontend or backend. A stage can share components with later stages; it must not rely on unbuilt optional features.

Deliverable contract

Create prototype/index.html, editable prototype/styles.css and prototype/app.js, plus fixture modules or embedded data as needed. Provide an offline bundle named prototype/Whiteboard-Academic-Prototype.html for review. Hash-style routing is acceptable for local HTML; preserve the W route semantics in a route manifest so later framework migration is straightforward. Do not overwrite the specification's REPORT.html or included original prototype.

Prefer a small router, shared shell, semantic components, domain records and pure rendering boundaries over one giant duplicated page per state. Keep CSS tokens independent so visual refinement does not rewrite grade logic. No build framework is required for the first HTML. If a receiving developer chooses tooling, record it and keep a readable offline artifact; dependencies must not make the design impossible to open.

Load local fixtures, no production endpoints. A scenario toolbar can select student/instructor/TA, course and error state. It belongs outside the product shell. A new role renders only permitted data. Clearly label the artifact “Prototype - fictional data.” Scenario storage may be local and resettable; it is not a secure grade system.

Every clickable app control must navigate, mutate sample state correctly, open a specified dialog or explain its bounded prototype limitation. Do not use a generic success toast for an unimplemented consequential action. Give local sample downloads real content and honest labels; do not claim they reached another system.

Build stages

StagePages and integrated outcomeExit check
0. FoundationW01-W06, W10, W13 and reusable shell/fixturesRole/course context, deep-link returns, session/permission states, light/dark and keyboard navigation work.
1. Teaching transactionW14-W24, W35-W40, W43-W44, W48-W49, W51-W53; bounded roster fixtureInstructor publishes one assignment; student selects/reviews/submits; TA reviews assigned work; instructor previews/releases; learner sees the right receipt and grade. Invalid and interrupted cases recover.
2. Assessment depthW25-W27, W41-W42, W45-W47, W50, W54, W57Quiz immutable attempts, timing/allowances, TA scope/expiry, rubric/manual override protection, groups, grading allocation and correction all connect.
3. Daily course lifeW07-W09, W11-W12, W28-W34, W55-W56Announcements, discussion, course/private calendars, reminders, activity, tools and help connect to the same course records. No private calendar leakage.
4. Course continuityW58-W60 and full W06 archive behaviorAttendance/insights use facts, copy/import excludes learner records, previews invalidate, prior term access is truthful.
5. Design QA and refinementAll required W pages/variantsReview completed coverage, responsive behavior, error recovery, keyboard/AT, privacy and text; document known gaps.
Optional, separately selectedO01-O03Awards/assistant cannot alter grades or expose hidden context and cannot block a required journey.

The page catalogue's priority describes functional importance; the stage table describes dependency-aware implementation order. Some core pages need a bounded version in Stage 1 and deeper variants later. Keep a checklist of fields/states still outstanding; never call a page complete because its default screenshot exists.

Acceptance matrix

For each page ID record source path, implemented controls, states tested, desktop/narrow screenshots when permitted, keyboard result, assistive-technology result where run, issues and owner design feedback. Keep these statuses separate: specified, HTML implemented, source checked, browser checked, accessibility reviewed, owner accepted. A source check never sets the other statuses to Passed.

Mandatory scenario checks

  1. Wrong account/institution cannot accept an invitation; valid repeated acceptance does not add a duplicate course role.
  2. An unpublished or prerequisite-locked material is not accessible through search or a copied link; permitted availability text is clear.
  3. File upload rejects a corrupt/unsupported/oversized example, preserves the other files, and retries without duplicate submission. Keyboard selection/reordering has equivalent controls.
  4. Closing review or toggling offline produces no receipt. Successful send creates one exact received attempt with person/group, files/pages, accepted time and reference.
  5. Starting another attempt preserves the old receipt; later assignment/quiz edits do not change submitted contents.
  6. All required questions must be reviewed before marking grading complete. A manual rubric override survives a bulk rule update.
  7. Changing recipient scope, score, comment, attempt or policy makes release preview stale. TA deep-link/action attempts to release are denied.
  8. Aisha's fixture learner/staff totals equal 84.50% / 85.17%. Held results never leak into W24, search, notifications or exports available to that learner.
  9. Invalid policy weights, duplicate item mapping, empty categories, zero-denominator and overlapping letter ranges show actionable errors; no NaN/Infinity grade appears.
  10. A group member's accepted attempt creates one group receipt with captured members; a later membership change preserves it. Individual grade override clearly names the affected learner.
  11. Grading allocations drive both TA queue and calendar. Revoking/expiring access blocks current saves, preserving attributed prior work without exposing other scopes.
  12. Published announcements appear in course and activity at the selected time. Drafts do not. Read state does not delete the announcement.
  13. A private work shift remains private across role switches. Moving/cancelling a course event updates both calendar views and supersedes its earlier reminder.
  14. Grade correction preserves prior release, shows old/new and reason, and changes the learner only after re-release. No direct-message inbox is invented.
  15. A copied course contains zero learners/grades/submissions. Import blockers remain inspectable; changing mapping invalidates the accepted preview.
  16. Reset a scenario twice and repeat the journey; state starts consistently and does not mix prior users, terms or attempts.

Visual and accessibility review

Review representative desktop widths, 768px and narrow 320/390px layouts; long labels and multiple data rows; 200% text and 400% browser zoom where appropriate; light/dark; keyboard-only; reduced motion; high contrast/forced colors; a relevant screen reader in the permitted environment. Test focus after modal close, save failure, navigation and dynamically revealed errors. Test timer announcements, contained tables and full text alternatives. Record exact browser/OS/AT versions and what actually ran.

First HTML does not need every device-native capability, real push/email, a camera capture service or live SSO. It does need accurate denied/unavailable states and usable alternatives. Do not interpret prototype success as storage correctness, security assurance, accessibility certification or institution acceptance.

Later frontend integration boundary

After visual approval, the frontend developer may map semantic routes/components to their chosen stack. Agree on API/data contracts for identity/course scope, conditional writes/version conflicts, pagination/filtering, upload acknowledgment, quiz time authority, immutable attempt/release records, permission failures and notification delivery. Design a service adapter boundary in the frontend; do not couple UI to global fixtures everywhere. Real records and authorization require a separately approved engineering plan.

No backend provider, database, hosting, AI vendor, first school or SIS/IdP is selected by this handoff. SSO/LTI/import labels remain neutral until an institutional partner confirms them.

Questions that remain for owner/institution

The HTML can use the proposed defaults while showing alternate scenarios. Before production, confirm: first institution and source roles; exact TA authoring/moderation permissions; upload formats/size and accessible alternatives; late penalties/dropped work/extra credit/rounding and letter boundaries; category and course-total publication; group membership/individual-grade disputes; quiz expiry/resume/accommodation policy; course archive/retention/download policy; meeting and reminder source authority; actual tool licenses; accessibility support path; and whether achievements or AI merit inclusion.

These questions do not block making the first HTML from this brief. They must not be disguised as universal rules or customer-validated requirements. Keep a decision log if the receiving developer changes a proposed default.

Readiness and non-goals

“All pages specified” is a handoff completeness check, not proof all product questions are solved. Method and interpretation

The review began with the project's accepted academic concepts and the coworker gap assessment, then examined public primary documentation for grading, groups, calendars, submission and accessibility. Shared/student and staff evidence tables record the domain sources. Duplicate URLs across tables are one source, not independent corroboration. Publication dates are recorded only when explicitly shown; search crawl dates are not publication dates.

The result is a proposed page/task/state inventory. Its priorities are product judgments. No real student work, class data, private PDF or school credentials were sent to search tools. No paid research APIs or private competitor accounts were used. The coworker's reported Blackboard frustration is retained as a workflow observation, while current official documentation establishes that weighting and groups are supported capabilities.

Local sources

The original design tokens/components, academic batch renderers, canonical S/P map, D1-D65 decisions, source contract and normalized coworker review informed the proposal. resources/README.md identifies exact included files and their SHA-256 provenance. Original sources are references, not a new production architecture. More complete proposed W specifications supersede their academic gaps for this handoff; they do not retroactively mark old designs/browser checks as implemented or passed.

Document 12 · Contract (history)

From resources/history/CONTRACT.md

Showcase source contract

Sources are concatenated into one offline HTML by showcase/build.mjs. No imports, network calls or runtime packages are required by the artifact. All data/effects are fictional. Preserve both archives; do not hand-edit generated HTML.

Modules and screens

  • core.js: canonical model, selectors, validation, helpers, render/action registry.
  • content.js: story chapters, six journey routes, shared hero renderer.
  • student.js: S01–S08, S10–S13 and student actions.
  • teaching.js: S09, S14–S23, grading/authoring/rollover actions.
  • campus.js: S24–S36, scheduling, events, organizations and support.
  • institution.js: S37–S40, reconciliation, migration and trust.
  • controller.js: browser event routing, focus, theme, local guides, URLs and downloads.
  • styles.css: offline semantic palette, layouts, responsive/reduced-motion behavior.

WB.reg(id,title,role,(state,h)=>html) registers a pure renderer. WB.render verifies no state mutation and temporarily sets the screen's sample actor, restoring the caller context afterward. Never initialize state inside a renderer.

WB.actions[name]=(state,params)=>({message?,go?,download?,errorPath?}) performs an intentional local change. download is {name,text}. go is a registered workspace ID. Prefix actions by module. Controllers announce at the destination and focus the requested error field. Action success must represent the corresponding model change.

Shared records

  • assignment: current assignment ID, title, due/close wall-clock values, publication, AI policy, five questions and sample attachments.
  • submission: Aisha's current attempt. submissions[personId]: other learners' attempts. Use WB.submissionFor(state,id) everywhere, rather than borrowing Aisha's pages.
  • Submission includes id,owner,status,attempt,pages,receipt; each page has id,tag,rotation,owner?,workVariant?. Editing received work starts a new draft and preserves an earlier receipt snapshot in history.
  • assessment.marks[personId]: scores for question IDs 1a,1b,2,3,4 with maxima 6,4,6,8,6. questionComments[personId][questionId] is answer-specific; comments[personId] is overall feedback.
  • reviewedQuestions[personId] tracks answer review; all required questions plus explicit completion are needed before the submission enters graded. released is separate.
  • teaching.releasePlan stores the approved preview payload/fingerprint; stale scope/content/attempt/eligibility cannot silently change the release. releaseSnapshots preserve the exact released version. Excused/missing/unreceived work is ineligible for numeric release.
  • teaching.modules drives student order/access; structured releaseAt and completed-module IDs drive availability. Reading labels/toggles use the active module’s own membership, never a shared completion boolean.
  • teaching.quizItems drives student answer controls; item types are Multiple choice, Numeric response and Written response, with optional options/answer. Draft answers are course.quizAnswers[itemId]. Submission deep-copies item text/options/reference answers, student answers and title/timing/release/deadline settings into course.quizSubmission; later author edits cannot change this receipt. The quiz owns teaching.quizDue, independent of assignment deadlines. Reset archives the receipt in course.quizHistory; explicit releases are keyed by attempt. New attempts require publication and use current authoring settings.
  • Allowances are {id,assignmentId,extraHours,extraMinutes}. Use WB.effectiveDates(state,personId) for assignment dates. Quiz time is separately scoped in teaching.quizAllowances; WB.quizExtraMinutes keeps it independent of assignment creation. Submitted attempts preserve their approved time allowance.
  • teaching.destinationCourse holds the actual separate copied modules/assignments/quizzes/tool-review record and no student data.
  • campus.meeting is the source-applied timetable. Proposals are separate from this record.
  • Published campus.event is separate from eventDraft. Date keys and start/end times are structured; approval fingerprints and existing commitments constrain publication.
  • campus.participation has confirmed records, aggregate other-confirmed count, ordered waitlist and sample pass. Use WB.personalCampusEvent for personal calendar context.
  • Use WB.studentSupportStatus for student-safe referral output; staff history/notes have separate scope.
  • Institution reconciliation, grade exports, migration rows/previews, portable export and access expiry are inspectable local records. No external system has received them.

Helpers and control semantics

WB.e escapes user text; WB.clone copies JSON-safe records. WB.audit records named actors and ordered times using WB.clock and the explicit fictional institution clock. WB.academicPolicy applies a course prohibition over the assignment rule; institution AI draft permission is separate.

WB.set(path,value) rejects unsafe prototype paths, invalid fields and inappropriate/locked edits. Invalid visible values block form actions instead of silently using an earlier valid model value. WB.fieldErrors is UI error state. Module actions also validate consequential transitions.

WB.actorFor(screen,state) labels the sample role. The controller sets this actor for actions; direct Node tests may leave it unset. This is a showcase role view, never production authentication or authorization.

HTML helpers: head renders h3 beneath a chapter h2; card renders h4. btn creates stable per-render IDs and data actions; go creates #Sxx navigation links. field/area/select provide labels and names; fields/areas associate errors. table supplies caption, column headers and a labeled scroll region. paper(question,rotation,owner,variant) renders owner-specific illustrative work, full text and an enlarged readable alternative inside a rotation-safe square stage. Escape dynamic content inserted into HTML bodies.

The controller avoids replacing unchanged panels, restores focus by control identity, supports native links/history and keeps guidance beside the active task. Actual browser acceptance is still separate from source/unit checks.

Scenario resets and checks

J1/J2 restore the academic dependency closure, preserving delivery preferences. J2 preserves an organized received Aisha submission only when it belongs to the original assignment. J3 resets the scheduling closure. WB.resetCampusJourney handles J4/J5. WB.resetInstitutionJourney handles the IT portion of J6 without regranting unrelated access; the controller separately resets course-copy state.

See showcase/README.md for build/check commands and 05_update_tracker.csv for acceptance evidence. Existing historical probes execute the v2 archive, not the revised modules. Never infer browser focus, clipping, console cleanliness, real-device performance or conformance from a pure renderer count.

Design decisions and open questions

Baseline 15 October 2026. These distinguish existing direction from decisions Claude must still work through.

Existing direction

  • LMS-first, coherent teaching transactions; campus coordination expands around that core.
  • Final-product vision includes 50 mapped destinations, with ten additions still labeled proposed.
  • Separate web and planned iPhone presentation; twelve dense staff destinations recommend web for bulk work.
  • Clean hierarchy, whitespace, restrained semantic color, realistic data and subtle optional motion. Preserve recognizable Whiteboard identity; use current showcase/atlas as references, not final accepted designs.
  • Status, authority, privacy and recoverability are design requirements. A pending booking cannot look confirmed; a queue cannot look like an accepted submission.
  • Existing showcase has local JavaScript/CSS sources and offline HTML output. No production framework or native architecture selected by this handoff.
