Q06.3Who provides technical support?The institution’s IT Service Desk.
Q06.4Second approver for vendor access?No: one administrator grants temporary, scoped, time-limited vendor access that can be closed early (D58).
Q06.5Who makes the canonical-record choice?As drawn in S38: the administrator chooses, with the official student-records source recommended, and the local record is flagged for the Registrar. Official data does not change (D57).
Q06.6Faculty sign-off for migration acceptance?No: the implementation administrator’s acceptance alone, as drawn.

16 Oct 2026 — visual review (owner, in chat)

After opening the previews in their own browser, the owner said: “everything looks great”. All 100 design targets move to Accepted in the tracker. This is the owner’s visual approval, not a structured test: browser, keyboard and screen-reader acceptance stays *Not run*, and native device acceptance waits for a build that isn’t authorized.

Decision log

Append date, decision, reason, affected screen IDs/platforms, owner/review evidence and any remaining question. The “proposed by Claude, not owner-reviewed” status lines below are kept as history: on 16 Oct 2026 the owner accepted D1–D58 (see Owner review). The screen visuals themselves are not yet owner-reviewed.

15 Oct 2026 — Batch 01: shared design system + student journey S01–S09 (web, planned iOS)

Status of every entry below: proposed by Claude, not owner-reviewed. Affects S01–S09 web/iOS now; intended as the default for later batches once accepted.

  • D1 Identity and colour. Keep Whiteboard teal (#007176 light, #5cc8c8 dark fill with dark label) as the only identity colour; neutrals move toward Apple system greys; iOS dark uses true-black grouped backgrounds. Focus ring is a separate blue so focus never reads as selection. Reason: continuity with the showcase, restraint, distinct focus. Static contrast: 63 token pairs (light, dark, iOS dark) meet 4.5:1 text / 3:1 non-text; lowest text pair 5.34:1. Rendered contrast unverified.
  • D2 Type. System font stack (SF Pro on Apple platforms) with Dynamic Type roles; web body 15 px, iOS body 17 pt; tabular figures for times/scores. A “Larger text” preview (+24%) is provided; reflow at real accessibility sizes is unverified.
  • D3 One status vocabulary (K.STATUS in batch01/kit.js): Not started, Draft · not submitted, Queued · not received, Received, Not received, Feedback not released, Feedback released, Feedback updated, Excused, Locked, Closed, Extension applied, Last known, Read-only, Not open yet, Instructor preview. Always icon + words. Queued and Received never share colour/icon; Held/Not released is neutral (nothing is wrong).
  • D4 Navigation. Web: sidebar (Today, Courses, Calendar, Updates; Campus: Events, Support) + top bar with Search P45 / Help P46 / Account P44, all still *proposed*. Narrow web collapses the sidebar to a menu and stacks columns — it stays a web page (no tab bar). Planned iOS: four tabs (Today, Courses, Calendar, Updates), account avatar in the nav bar; Search/Help placement on iOS is still open. Course sections are links (deep-linkable pages), not ARIA tabs.
  • D5 Preview format. Editable sources design/system/*.css, design/batch01/*.js; node design/build.mjs embeds the S01–S09 briefs and routes from showcase/app_map/*.json and writes one offline design/preview/batch01_student_journey.html. No framework, no network assets. iPhone frames are HTML illustrations, not a native build.
  • D6 Truthful submission states. Web cannot background-queue; it says so (S06 offline, S07 queued). Planned iOS may queue but shows “Queued · not received” until server acknowledgment; only then S08 “Received”. Interrupted shows “Not submitted” with no reference number.
  • D7 Review before send. Scan/upload never submits; S07 confirmation restates attempt, pages and coverage. Editing a received attempt opens a copy (Attempt 2) with the original receipt preserved.
  • D8 Camera permission. Pre-permission explainer, then the OS/browser prompt; denial makes Photos/Files/upload the primary path and Settings secondary.
  • D9 Feedback privacy. Today/notifications say feedback exists but never show the score. Held feedback shows receipt facts only (no grading progress). Re-release names the change (old → new) and keeps the prior snapshot. Excused is distinct from zero/missing. Downstream record acknowledgment is a neutral notice that does not make released feedback look provisional.
  • D10 Dates. US format with explicit time zone (“Fri, Oct 16 · 11:59 pm ET”); personal (allowance) dates lead, course dates shown secondary.
  • D11 Added design states (not new routes): S04 syllabus view, S05 choose-method sheet, S07 confirm and queued-offline. Each is labelled “added” in the preview with a reason.

Remaining questions for the owner: accept/adjust D1–D11; iOS Search/Help placement; whether S05 “Message instructor” (closed state) should exist given communication scope (coverage area 8) is undecided; whether a regraded release should notify the student.

16 Oct 2026 — Batch 02: access/arrival (P41–P44) + instructor authoring (S14–S16, P47–P49)

Status: proposed by Claude, not owner-reviewed. Batch 02 was started on the user’s “continue” instruction *before* the owner reviewed Batch 01, so it builds on D1–D11 as still-unaccepted defaults; if D1–D11 change, Batch 02 inherits the change through the shared kit/CSS.

  • D12 Access shell. P41–P43 use a focused page with no product navigation (web) and no tab bar (iOS) until identity and role are known. Whiteboard never asks for a password; the school’s identity provider owns credentials and recovery. Hand-off names the school, the exact sign-in host and the return destination.
  • D13 iOS sign-in uses the system authentication session (Apple-owned prompt, then a secure system sheet). Shown as an illustration only; no native build.
  • D14 Invitations show full details only to the intended, signed-in recipient; the wrong account sees a masked address. Expired/used links never create duplicate access; replacement is a request to the inviter. Sample invitation is a TA invite (Maya Chen).
  • D15 First use is three steps (confirm details → preferences → first task), skippable and resumable; roles come from records, the person only chooses where to land. iOS asks for notification permission only after delivery choices are explained. Added state: P43 “Preferences step”.
  • D16 Account (P44). Editable vs institution-managed fields are visually and semantically distinct (read-only, dashed, “Managed by institution”); pronouns default blank; photo changes go to review while the current photo stays. Sessions and delegated access (calendar feed) are separate lists. iOS Account also hosts the proposed Search (P45) and Help (P46) entries — still the open placement question.
  • D17 Staff workspace shell. Web sidebar: Teaching, Grading, Calendar, Updates + course tools (Builder, Files, Rubrics, People, Next term). iOS staff tabs: Teaching, Grading, Calendar, Updates. Staff avatar colour differs from student (purple-grey) as a secondary cue only.
  • D18 Validation pattern. Field-level error beside the field (aria-invalid + describedby) + a rail summary whose items move focus to the field; publish stays visible but unavailable with its reason; checks announce “Blocks publishing / Warning / Passed” as text. Errors block, warnings don’t.
  • D19 Student preview has its own purple bar (“Viewing as a student · nothing is recorded”) with a direct return, on web and iOS; preview shows only what publication, dates and prerequisites allow.
  • D20 Change after publish. Editing published/in-use work shows a quantified learner-impact panel before applying: receipts, submitted pages and quiz-attempt snapshots never change; quizzes and rubrics version (v3 → v4); in-use rubric changes require an impact preview and a future-only vs re-score choice (re-score routes to grading review, S17).
  • D21 Files. Replace creates a version (history and usage locations kept); uploading/processing/failed are distinct statuses; an asset without an accessible alternative can be inserted only with the issue flagged into the page’s checks.
  • D22 Desktop-recommended destinations (P47, P49). iOS shows a mapped subset (block list / rubric summary, focused sheets, read-only learner preview) plus a “Best on a computer” card with the web link. This is a presentation choice, not a native-parity decision.
  • D23 Lifecycle scenarios. Where map states span a lifecycle (S14 draft→published, S15 draft→changed), states are drawn on the same record with scenario dates (e.g. S14 draft states dated before term, Aug 24). P49 uses two rubrics from one library: a new “Free-body diagram quality” (draft/invalid/ready) and the in-use “Kinematics problem-solving” (in use/change), whose criteria match Aisha’s S09 feedback.
  • D24 Build/check format extended. design/batches.mjs registers batches; node design/build.mjs [batch] writes one page per batch; node design/tools/check_batch.mjs [batch] checks each. Cross-batch links (e.g. S14 → S03) open the other batch page at that state. Shared-kit edits made for this: iOS shell accepts a custom tab set; links resolve cross-batch; the S01 account avatar now opens P44 (route S01→P44 now has a control); controller supports focus-to-field buttons.

Remaining questions for the owner (in addition to Batch 01’s): accept/adjust D12–D24; is a TA invitation the right sample for P42 (vs. a student course join); should iOS staff have a Grading tab at all before S17 is designed; may an in-use rubric change ever re-score already-*released* work, or only unreleased grading.

16 Oct 2026 — Batch 03: quiz, discussion, calendar, updates (S10–S13) + grading and release (S17–S20)

Status: proposed by Claude, not owner-reviewed. Started on the user’s “continue”, before owner review of Batches 01–02; inherits D1–D24 unaccepted.

  • D25 Graded ≠ released. Staff-complete reviews are “Graded · staff only” (purple/accent, check icon); learner-visible results are “Released” (green). The gradebook shows a staff calculation and a separate “Learner sees” column, so a graded-but-unreleased score never looks published.
  • D26 Grading workspace (S17). Web: roster | learner page | score/rubric/comment panel; the question selector drives all three. Saved scores do not count as a completed review; “Mark review complete” stays disabled with the number of unreviewed questions. Missing work has no score field at all. TA after access ends: read-only, saved work kept, names who can restore access. Three panes need ~1240 px of app width; below that the roster becomes a horizontal picker row (unverified in a browser). iOS: learner title + question picker above the page, grading in a sheet — urgent review only, not a parity claim.
  • D27 Rubric rule changes (S18). Edits are previewed as an impact table (learner, level, score now → after, effect) before Apply. Manual scores are never overwritten by a rule change. Only the instructor applies; a TA can propose (Apply disabled with reason). Applying versions the rubric (v2 → v3). Released work (PS3, v1) is listed as unchanged — this avoids, but does not settle, the open question on re-scoring released work.
  • D28 Gradebook statuses (S19). Not graded = excluded; Missing = 0 after close; Excused = removed from denominator; Graded = staff calculation only; Released = both. Each state is explained in a rail for the focused cell, with the arithmetic shown.
  • D29 Release (S20). Steps Scope → Exceptions → Preview → Release. The preview is the exact per-learner payload (attempt, receipt, score, rubric version, comments). Any change after preview makes it stale and blocks release until refreshed. Web release needs an explicit confirmation checkbox; iOS uses a final confirmation step. Post-release edits become a held draft with old → new; releasing creates a new snapshot (R2) and keeps R1 — the same records Batch 01’s S09 “re-released” state shows. Institution record acknowledgment is separate and neutral (S38 later).
  • D30 Quiz attempt (S10). Rules first: window, personal time (allowance named, separate from assignment extensions), attempts, release rule. Answers save per item; offline answers are labelled “Saved on this device · not sent” and Submit waits for a connection; the timer is described honestly (it keeps running). The submission receipt promises that questions and answers are kept together as a snapshot. Held results show no scores, keys or progress.
  • D31 Course conversation (S11). Every contribution shows name, role chip (staff chips purple) and time; the composer states who you post as and who can see it. Locked threads remove reply controls rather than disabling them. The map state “course not published” is drawn as the Module 4 discussion before it opens.
  • D32 Calendar and updates (S12, S13). Every calendar item names its source; a delayed source keeps last-known items, labelled; changes show old → new with who/when. Device-calendar sync is an optional switch with its own permission. Updates link to the changed record, never show scores, and say that delivery preferences change future email/alerts only; iOS keeps system notification permission and Whiteboard delivery switches as separate controls.
  • D33 Handoffs and shared-kit edits. Student→staff routes (S08→S17, S10→S16) are explained in words with data-handoff, never linked; the checker now accepts that for handoff routes. Student Calendar/Updates tabs and nav, course Quizzes/Discussion links and the staff Grading/Calendar entries now open Batch 03 pages. Staff “Updates” stays a note: S13 is the student feed and no staff feed is mapped. The staff shell accepts another signed-in staff member (used for the TA views).

Remaining questions for the owner (in addition to earlier batches’): accept/adjust D25–D33; does a staff Updates feed need its own destination; should Missing appear to learners before the next release (S19 currently shows learners the released view only); quiz-time allowance shown to the learner by name (“1.5× quiz time”) — acceptable wording/privacy; can a TA release, or only the instructor (drawn instructor-only); should regraded releases notify the learner (still open from Batch 01).

16 Oct 2026 — Batch 04: course operations (S21–S23) + academic scheduling (S24–S25)

Status: proposed by Claude, not owner-reviewed. Started on the user’s “continue”, before owner review of Batches 01–03; inherits D1–D33 unaccepted.

  • D34 Course people and permissions (S21). Staff and students in roster tables with role, access status, end date and the action beside each person. A course-role permission table answers in words (Yes / No / Propose only / Assigned work only). It matches D27 (TAs propose rubric changes) and D29 (release is instructor-only). Course roles never carry over to other courses or institution accounts. Institution access is S37’s job, so it is explained as a handoff and never linked. An invitation is not access: nothing is visible to the invitee until they accept while signed in (P42). Expired access blocks course actions, keeps saved work and offers Extend access with a named date. This is the restoration that S17 “access expired” points to.
  • D35 Revocation. Revoking access opens a review (web dialog, iOS sheet) that names the person, role, course and term. It lists what ends and what is kept, and takes an optional staff-only reason. Revoked records stay: earlier scores remain attributed and released feedback is unchanged. This review is an added design state (S21 “Revoke review”) with its reason recorded.
  • D36 Allowances are operational records. Each record stores what changes, which work, the personal dates or multiplier, who recorded it and when, and a basis label with at most a reference number (e.g. Accessibility Services AS-…). It never holds private or medical documentation. All course staff see the adjusted timing; only the instructor sees the basis reference. S17’s Excuse/Extension buttons now open S21. Tomás Rivera’s PS4 extension (recorded Mon, Oct 19, after S17 showed him Missing) is the sample. The route to S15 shows the personal date in the assignment editor.
  • D37 Course copy (S22). The steps are Select → Dates → Preview → Copy. A “Never copied” list names the learner data that is excluded: people, submissions, scores and feedback, discussions, allowances and attendance. Dates shift by a stated rule (+21 weeks, weekdays kept), and source and destination dates sit side by side. Dates that land in a break are flagged for checking, not moved silently. An unsupported external tool blocks the copy until the instructor picks a placeholder page or leaves it out. “Approved tool” is shown as unavailable, with who reviews tool requests. The copy needs an explicit review checkbox on a current preview, and any change makes the preview stale. Applying creates a separate draft course with zero learners and leaves the source unchanged.
  • D38 Insights are facts, not predictions (S23). The page shows three separate records: not submitted before close (named, with allowance status; excused learners not counted), module completion (three named counts) and attendance (each entry with its source). There is no composite score, risk label or prediction. An attendance correction quotes the request and records the corrected status, reason, who and when. The original entry is kept in history. When a source is delayed, entries are labelled “last known”, and an unentered session is not counted as absent. Referral to advising (S35) is a handoff.
  • D39 Scheduling-office shell and timetable (S24). The new shell has Timetable, Change reviews and Find a room (S26, later). The role and term are shown, and iOS gets matching tabs. The timetable is a read-only copy of the institution scheduling source, with the system, status and last refresh always visible. Conflicts attach to the specific meeting, with text and evidence (a Facilities notice). Proposals appear inside the meeting as dashed “Proposed · not applied” notes while the source room stays shown. A department scheduler (e.g. Dr. Diane Reyes for Physics, from P41/P43) is assumed to see the same page filtered to their department and to propose but not approve. That scope is an assumption to confirm.
  • D40 Approve ≠ apply (S25). Each room option shows its constraint verdict, and rejected alternatives stay visible: a room that is too small, and one that overlaps another class. A constraint evidence table compares current and proposed. Submitting and approving are both stated not to change the timetable. Apply source copy is a separate, acknowledged step. The change counts as “Applied” only when the refreshed source copy reflects it. Learners hear about it through Calendar (S12) only after that point, as a handoff. The MATH 220 move to Keene Center 105 (applied Thu, Oct 15 · 7:30 am) is the same change S12 shows learners at 7:40 am.
  • D41 Shared edits for Batch 04. The staff sidebar gains Insights (S23), and People and Next term now open S21 and S22. The S14 course tools and iOS Course rows now link S21–S23. P41 and P43 scheduling roles now open S24. S17’s Excuse/Extension buttons open S21. The design-system nav table gains a Scheduling office row. kit4.js adds the scheduling shell, labelled radio/checkbox helpers and a timeline helper.

Remaining questions for the owner (in addition to earlier batches’): accept/adjust D34–D41. Can a TA record allowances (drawn: no)? Should the learner see the allowance basis label? Should attendance be recorded at all, and is a learner-initiated correction request in scope (communication scope is still undecided)? Who owns the “approved tool” list for course copy? Should a department scheduler approve within their own department, or only the registrar? Does Whiteboard ever write to the scheduling source, or only record that the registrar applied the change there (drawn as “Apply source copy” followed by waiting for the refreshed copy, with no live integration)?

16 Oct 2026 — Batch 05: campus spaces (S26–S27) + campus life (S28–S33)

Status: proposed by Claude, not owner-reviewed. Started on the user’s “continue”, before owner review of Batches 01–04; inherits D1–D41 unaccepted.

  • D42 Campus navigation. The student web sidebar’s Campus group becomes Events (S28), Organizations (S29) and Support (S34, later). The student iPhone tab bar gains a fifth tab, Campus; this changes every student iOS frame in Batches 01–03. Organization officers keep the student shell plus a role-scoped organization section (home, event drafts, find a room, room requests, check-in, handoff). An event operator sees only that event’s check-in. Event Services and Student Activities staff get a campus-operations shell (Room requests, Find a room, Event reviews; iOS tabs Requests, Reviews, Rooms).
  • D43 Room search checks the whole interval (S26). Every result repeats every requirement as met or not met, in text, and states its availability for the full start-to-end interval, including setup and teardown. Unavailable rooms stay listed with the conflicting booking named. Requirements are never dropped to find a match; “No full match” explains what each closest option lacks. Choosing a room is not a request.
  • D44 Request ≠ approval ≠ confirmation (S27). A request moves Draft → Requested → Approved · not confirmed → Confirmed in source. Approval records a fingerprint of the exact details, and any change to them returns the request to review. Confirmation is a separate step: the approver records the reservation system’s confirmation number, and Whiteboard never books a room. A single date is cancelled on its own and the series is kept. Calendar shows the request with the same status words (new S12 requester state).
  • D45 Participation status (S28). Place confirmed, Full, Waitlisted (#n of m) and Cancelled are text badges on every row and in the details. Capacity is a sentence (“48 of 60 places confirmed · 12 left”) before the bar. A waitlist position creates no pass and no calendar entry. Cancelled events stay visible to people who held a place, with who, when and why, and their actions are removed. Only approved, published versions appear in discovery.
  • D46 Organization ownership (S29, S30, S33). Drafts, room requests, funding requests and files belong to the organization, never to an officer’s account. A revision is an organization draft beside the unchanged published version. Capacity can’t drop below confirmed places. “Send for review” needs valid fields and every dependency at least requested. The handoff needs an assignment, the incoming officer’s acceptance and every required item done. Until then the outgoing officer stays in the role. Afterwards the outgoing officer keeps membership and the organization keeps the work.
  • D47 Independent dependency owners (S31). Room (Event Services), funding (Student Activities Fund) and event review (Student Activities) each show their owner and status. A reviewer can read the room and funding decisions but can’t change them. An open dependency disables Approve, naming that dependency. Approve ≠ publish: approval fingerprints the revision; publishing replaces version 1 and notifies the confirmed attendees.
  • D48 Offline check-in is not attendance until synced (S32). Check-ins made offline read “Queued on this device · not synced”, and the event total counts synced records only. Reconciliation shows each queued record’s result. A duplicate keeps the earlier check-in and names the device and time. An ineligible result gives a reason and what to say, with no operator override. Operator scope is one event for a set time. Manual lookup covers a denied camera.
  • D49 Student pass (added S32 state). The pass shows a decorative code, a short typed or spoken code as its accessible equivalent, and the event, time, place and status. It works offline and needs no calendar permission. Wallet is out of scope.
  • Shared edits for Batch 05. These close the earlier “later batch” notes. K.web takes who and groups. S01’s Explore events and campus row open S28. S12’s campus event and S13’s campus update open S28. S12 gains a requester state (route S12→S27). S24’s Inspect room options and the scheduling Find a room link open S26 (the S26 preview follows the event scenario; a note says so). The design-system nav table now lists campus navigation.

Remaining questions for the owner (in addition to earlier batches’):

  • Accept or adjust D42–D49.
  • Is a fifth student tab right, or should Campus live under Today?
  • Who records the reservation confirmation: Event Services by hand (drawn) or a source integration?
  • Should a waitlist offer expire, and after how long (none drawn)?
  • Can the president, the adviser or Student Activities complete a handoff?
  • Are guests and walk-ins configured per event?
  • Does attendance reconciliation feed any record beyond the event?

16 Oct 2026 — Batch 06: student support (S34–S36), institution operations (P50, S37–S40), shared tools (P45–P46)

Status: proposed by Claude, not owner-reviewed. Started on the user’s “continue”, before owner review of Batches 01–05; inherits D1–D49 unaccepted. This batch completes all 50 destinations × 2 platforms as design drafts.

  • D50 Support placement. On the web, Support is the third item in the student Campus group (it now opens S34). On iPhone, Support lives under the Campus tab and the Today card; no sixth tab is added. Technical help (P46) is always a separate link, never a support service.
  • D51 Search and help entry on iPhone. P45 is reached from a nav-bar search button (Today, Campus) and from Account (P44); P46 is reached from Account and from contextual error links. Neither gets a tab. Opening a search result pushes its destination; Back returns to the kept query.
  • D52 Referrals share facts, never judgments (S34–S35). A referral carries the course, one observed fact and a note the student will read. It never carries grades, scores, submissions, attendance, allowances, private notes, diagnoses or risk labels. Both recipient views are previewed before sending. Destination and student-visible note are required. Corrections keep the earlier wording in the referrer’s history only. Teaching assistants have no referral permission (drawn: instructor or adviser only).
  • D53 One case, two views (S36). Staff notes and the student-safe status are separate regions of the same case. Every state names who owns the next step, including “no one”, and the student status stays truthful when a case is unowned. Redirect and return-to-queue keep ordered history. The service can’t edit a referrer’s text; it asks the referrer (S35 handoff). Added S36 state: “Student view”, for arrivals from S13 and S34.
  • D54 Search never hints at hidden material (P45). Results come only from what the person can open. Restricted items are not shown, counted or hinted at; the empty state says what search covers and who to ask. Each result names its source; archived items are labelled before opening.
  • D55 Technical requests list their diagnostics (P46). Each diagnostic item is an editable checkbox, with a “never included” line (pages, answers, grades, messages). Photos/Files permission is asked only when adding an attachment. A technical request never changes an assignment receipt. Vendor access for a request is an institution decision (S37).
  • D56 Institution administration shell (P50, S37–S40). One administration shell with Initial setup, People/access/records, Connections, Migration rehearsal and Trust & AI controls. All five recommend desktop; the iPhone frames are read-first subsets with a “Best on a computer” note. No native parity is decided.
  • D57 Sources of record and acknowledgments (P50, S38). The student records system stays official for people, enrollment and final grades. Setup records each source owner’s acceptance, and rehearsal is blocked until the Registrar accepts. A grade transfer reads Validated · not sent → Acknowledged / Rejected by source, row by row, with the source’s reason quoted. Duplicate people are resolved by an explicit canonical choice; nothing merges silently. Every connection is labelled “Sample refresh · not live”.
  • D58 Acceptance binds a fingerprint; controls are intentions (S39–S40). Migration acceptance names one exact preview fingerprint and goes stale when the source or mapping changes. A rehearsal never implies a production migration, and learner submissions and grades are not migrated. AI drafting allowed at the institution never overrides a stricter course policy. Data-use and accessibility entries describe intentions, with no compliance or certification claim. Exports are local fictional samples. Temporary vendor support access names its purpose, scope and window, and can be closed early.
  • Shared edits for Batch 06. These close every remaining “later batch” note. Student, staff, scheduling and operations shells: Search opens P45 and Help opens P46. Campus › Support opens S34. S01 Find support, S09 Ask for learning support and S13’s support update now link S34/S36. P41/P43 administrator choices open S37/P50. S14’s implementation acceptance and S20’s institution record are S37/S38 handoffs in words. Stale notes for S10–S14 and S17 (designed in Batches 02–03) are now links.

Remaining questions for the owner (in addition to earlier batches’):

  • Accept or adjust D50–D58.
  • Who can create referrals: instructors and advisers only (drawn), or TAs too?
  • Should a student be able to see and decline a referral before the service acts?
  • Who provides technical support: the institution’s IT Service Desk (drawn), or the vendor directly?
  • Should vendor support access need a second approver?
  • Is a canonical-record choice the IT team’s to make, or the Registrar’s?
  • Should migration acceptance need faculty sign-off as well as the implementation administrator’s?

16 Oct 2026 — Delegated decisions: project-level questions (D59–D64)

Status: chosen by Claude under owner delegation (owner, 16 Oct 2026: “all the decisions u are asking from me, i will ask u to choose the best ones”). Not owner-reviewed individually; the owner can reopen any of them.

  • D59 No direct messaging. Whiteboard has no direct-message inbox or chat. Learners reach staff through course context instead: the course discussion (S11), support (S34) and typed requests that staff decide on. S05’s closed state replaces the “Message instructor” placeholder with “Request more time…”. It sends a request to the instructor with the assignment attached; a request is not an extension, and any extension shows as the learner’s personal date (S21). Announcements stay in Updates (S13). Reason: the coverage review says to reuse notifications and course context before adding another inbox. A typed request keeps the record, the authority and the outcome in one place, and avoids an unmoderated private channel. Affects S05 (web, iOS).
  • D60 What staff can do on iPhone. For the twelve desktop-recommended destinations, iPhone is for reading and reviewing, single-record actions and protective actions. Bulk changes, or commits that need side-by-side comparison, go to the web with “Best on a computer”. The drawn frames already follow this rule, so no design changes. P47: edit one block and fix accessibility gaps; Publish on the web. P49: read and attach an existing rubric; criterion edits on the web. S18: wording-only changes; score-affecting rule changes apply on the web. S19: read, and open one learner’s work; no bulk edits. S22: review and resolve exceptions; the copy runs only against a current, reviewed preview. S24: read the timetable and propose one change. S25: approve one change and record the source copy; comparing many changes is on the web. P50: setup status and issue owners; setup steps on the web. S37: look up people and close support access now (protective). S38: read exceptions; canonical-record choices on the web. S39: read the rehearsal and its exceptions; acceptance is recorded on the web through S37. S40: read controls and turn a control off (protective); turning anything on stays on the web.
  • D61 No workspace splits or merges. All 50 destination IDs stay as they are. Variants such as group work, recurrence exceptions, organization registration and renewal, or connector setup are states inside the existing workspaces, not new pages. Reason: every batch fitted its scope into the mapped destinations without strain.
  • D62 No new standalone routes. Regrade detail stays in the learner’s feedback history (S09) and the gradebook (S19). Organization flows stay in S29, S30 and S33. Direct messaging is not added (D59). Reason: each is a variant of a workspace that already exists, and a new route would duplicate its authority rules.
  • D63 First school, records system and sign-in are working assumptions. Designs stay system-neutral: a generic “student records” source and institution single sign-on, with no vendor or protocol named, and every connection labelled as a sample. No first-school segment, records system or identity provider is chosen. That needs partner discovery and must not be presented as a requirement or a customer.
  • D64 Acceptance environment. Visual, keyboard and screen-reader acceptance is done by user-assisted inspection: the owner opens the previews in their own browser and shares screenshots or observations, and Claude triages and fixes. Claude doesn’t bypass the local-file restriction. Device acceptance waits for a native build, which is not authorized.

16 Oct 2026 — Click-through prototype (D65)

Status: requested by the owner (“make the whole software in html just like a prototype … different versions like student, teacher, school workers”); approach chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

  • D65 Prototype built from the accepted designs, not redrawn. design/prototype/Whiteboard-Prototype.html renders the same 50 screen sources full-size, so it can’t drift from what was accepted (all 508 renders were checked identical in one combined page). It adds 8 roles (student, instructor, TA, organization officer, scheduling office, Event Services & Student Activities, support staff, institution IT & administration), 24 guided tours that cross roles where the work does, a Web/iPhone switch, a state picker labelled “Other situations”, and buttons that open the staff side of a student→staff handoff. The designs keep data-handoff as words, and only the prototype shell adds that button. It is click-through only: typing isn’t saved, and controls without a designed destination show their note. Every page is labelled as a prototype with fictional data. Sharing is the owner’s call: a single offline file, or a private Artifact link if asked.

Document 14 · State checklist (history)

From resources/history/state_checklist.md

Design coverage beyond the primary screen count

Use the per-screen states, web, ios, actions and incoming/outgoing transitions in the app-map JSON as the first brief. This checklist adds shared coverage; not every state applies to every target. Record justified N/A decisions rather than drawing meaningless states.

Every destination/platform

  • [ ] Purpose, actor, institution/course context and information hierarchy are clear.
  • [ ] Entry, next action, back/cancel and deep-link return are specified; multi-role people keep the correct context.
  • [ ] Default/loading/empty/error/validation/success and unavailable/no-access states are specified where relevant.
  • [ ] Destructive actions, unsaved changes, confirmations/undo and pending approvals have explicit behavior.
  • [ ] Shared account/search/preferences/technical help preserve original workspace and role on return.
  • [ ] Light/dark, readable contrast, visible focus, labels/error associations, keyboard order and reduced motion are considered.
  • [ ] Desktop, narrow web and iPhone navigation are distinguished; long content, large text, safe areas and keyboard obstruction are considered.
  • [ ] Role handoffs show responsible person/team, record status and authoritative source. Navigation does not grant permission.
  • [ ] Design source, preview, state coverage and actual verification evidence are recorded in the tracker.

Critical journeys

  • Access: wrong institution, SSO return/failure/expiry, mismatched/expired invitation, role context and onboarding recovery.
  • Submission: camera/file permission denial, accessible alternative, unreadable/reordered pages, progress/interruption/retry, draft versus accepted receipt, preserved prior attempt and truthful offline status.
  • Assessment: publication/availability, timed/autosaved work, accommodations, immutable attempt snapshot, staff-only references, held versus released results and correction/regrade behavior.
  • Teaching: draft/publish/student preview, resource versions/alternatives, prerequisite/release constraints, TA scope, answer-specific feedback and exact release preview/snapshot.
  • Campus: room request versus authoritative booking, time/capacity/accessibility constraints, revisions that invalidate approvals, RSVP/waitlist/pass eligibility, guests and check-in reconciliation.
  • Support: student-safe status, restricted staff context, assignment/escalation, correction history and accountable next action.
  • IT: tenant/role scope, revocation/expiry, sync exceptions/retry, migration preview acceptance/staleness and honest trust/AI controls.

Eight expanded areas from the coverage review

Specify these inside existing destinations before deciding they need extra routes:

  1. S11: announcement authoring/draft/schedule/publication, threads and moderation.
  2. S05/S15/S17/S21: groups, section-specific work, file rules, learner exceptions and controlled revisions.
  3. S09/S19/S20: course-wide grades, correction/regrade lifecycle and export.
  4. S10/S16: complete quiz authoring, autosave/time/recovery and attempt versions/history.
  5. S29/S30/S31/S33: organization registration/renewal, configurable forms, rosters/roles, funding request history; formal finance remains external.
  6. S26/S27/S28/S30/S31/S32: own events/bookings, details, recurrence exceptions, approval, passes and accessibility/guest flows.
  7. S37–S40/P50: initial versus ongoing configuration, terms/archives, connector setup/mapping, audit and evidence.
  8. S11/S13: communication scope. A new direct-message inbox is undecided, not automatically a committed feature.

Evidence boundaries

Source checks validate structure/state logic. Browser inspection validates rendered behavior in that environment. Native simulator/device testing validates that build/environment. Owner review accepts a design direction. Keep these separate. No compliance or certification claim follows from this checklist.

Research findings that affect the recommendations

Grading and group work come first

Blackboard documents points, weighted and custom overall-grade calculations, with item/category weights and calculation details for students. Whiteboard's opportunity is understandable configuration and trustworthy calculations; “Blackboard cannot weight grades” is not a supported competitive claim. [Overall Grade Column](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/instructor/en/grading/grading-setup/grade-columns/overall-grade-column.html), [Course Grades](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/student/en/grades/course-grades.html).

Proposed validation: configure Assignments 10%, Exam 1 25%, Exam 2 25% and Final 40%; map assessments; reconcile an independently calculated student example. Specify empty categories, missing versus ungraded versus excused items, equal versus point-proportional weighting, rounding, extra credit, letter boundaries and policy changes. Keep staff drafts separate from released learner results. These are proposed acceptance cases, not a new adopted grading policy.

Blackboard supports course group sets and assessment use, and documents effects of membership changes. That supports the need to design the complete transaction rather than only a grouping dropdown. [Create and Manage Groups](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/instructor/en/interact-with-students/groups/create-and-manage-groups.html).

Proposed validation: create groups manually or randomly, find unassigned learners, assign one assessment, let a member submit for the group, show the same receipt to authorized members, then grade and release. Decide individual overrides, late join/withdrawal, membership snapshots, resubmission and TA assignment scope before treating it as complete. Keep grading groups distinct from staff navigation groups and course sections.

Calendar, communication and activity should share records

Blackboard documents personal events and a course-only calendar, including instructor-added office hours and schedules. Google documents personal notification settings and recurring-event edits. These are useful bounded references for the planner. Neither commits Whiteboard to Google Calendar feature parity. [Blackboard Calendar](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/student/en/getting-started/calendar.html), [Google notifications](https://support.google.com/calendar/answer/37242), [Google recurring events](https://support.google.com/calendar/answer/37115).

Proposed validation: publish an exam and office-hour series; see them in course and combined views without duplicates; add a private work shift; edit one recurring occurrence; change the exam time and invalidate its old reminder. Private items must not become visible to professors/TAs. Test time zones and notification permission denial. Grading-task records should drive the TA calendar and work queue together.

Blackboard distinguishes announcement creation, scheduling and posting from its activity stream. Its instructor stream includes grading work. Whiteboard can extend S03/S11/S13 and role-aware S12 instead of introducing duplicate feeds. [Announcements](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/instructor/en/interact-with-students/announcements.html), [Student Activity Page](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/student/en/getting-started/activity-page.html), [Instructor Activity Page](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/instructor/en/getting-started/activity-page.html).

Quiz integrity needs a separate decision

MDN documents visibility and focus signals; they describe browser state, not what a student did elsewhere. Its fullscreen guidance explicitly permits user/browser exit. Respondus describes a separate custom browser for application restrictions. This supports a distinction between ordinary web telemetry and a controlled exam environment; it does not prove any system eliminates cheating. [Page Visibility API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Page_Visibility_API), [Fullscreen guide](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fullscreen_API/Guide), [Respondus LockDown Browser](https://web.respondus.com/he/lockdownbrowser/).

Recommendation, not an adopted policy: never label a focus-loss event “cheating” or automatically erase/cancel the whole attempt from a simple counter. Preserve saved work, disclose the chosen policy, distinguish connectivity/device interruptions, provide accessible recovery and staff review. Evaluate a secure-browser integration only if a partner requires it, with device, accessibility, support and cost implications. “Mouse tracking” is inaccurate terminology for tab/window visibility monitoring.

Tools, achievements and AI require clear scope

Software access depends on the institution, role and license. Google's school-account documentation distinguishes feature access by license; Cornell's service matrix is one institutional example of role-specific access. Whiteboard should show verified eligibility and access instructions, not promise Adobe/Gemini is universally free. [Google school accounts](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/14620100?co=DASHER._Family%3DEducation&hl=en), [Cornell role-based services](https://it.cornell.edu/netids/it-services-available-your-role-cornell).

Blackboard's Achievements feature awards course badges against criteria. Proposed Whiteboard awards should be optional and separate from official grades unless an explicit grading rule says otherwise. Their existence elsewhere is not evidence that the first school needs them. [Achievements](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/instructor/en/interact-with-students/achievements.html).

Blackboard's AVA illustrates a course assistant controlled by institution/instructor settings and scoped to student-visible content, with accuracy limitations. For Whiteboard, a later FAQ/navigation assistant could use published materials with citations and a staff escalation path. It must not reveal answer keys, held grades or other learners' data, bypass a course AI prohibition, or autonomously change grades. Provider, handling, evaluation and operating cost remain undecided. [AVA student documentation](https://help.anthology.com/blackboard/student/en/course-content-and-materials/ava-ai-virtual-assistant.html).

Proposed backlog order

These priorities are review judgments, not owner-approved implementation scope or delivery estimates.

  1. Core academic completeness: AR10 configurable grading policy; AR12 student course grades; AR13 groups and group assignments. Design them together so the learner outcome matches staff setup and release rules.
  2. Daily academic work: AR04 announcement authoring; AR06 course calendar; AR11 TA grading calendar; AR01 reminders; AR09 semester activity history. Follow with AR02 private planning and AR05 complete term/archive navigation.
  3. Academic access convenience: AR08 Tools directory and course-specific software access. Do not expand into institution administration to provide a useful directory.
  4. Optional/discovery work: AR14 achievements and AR15 assistant. AR07 assessment integrity needs feasibility/policy discovery before a feature decision; technical review should occur before promising restrictions.
  5. Preserve: AR03 no direct messaging, existing authority boundaries, immutable receipts and release snapshots, scoped TAs and truthful pending/offline states.

Candidate placement uses existing S02/S03/S05/S07-S13/S15-S17/S19/S21 and shared tools. Do not silently add destinations or change the 50-destination baseline: D61/D62 remain the recorded decisions. A design pass must explicitly review any route addition that becomes necessary. The wider campus work remains saved and outside the current focus.

Document 17 · README

From README.md

Whiteboard academic web app: frontend handoff

Start with REPORT.html for the complete readable brief, or give Claude Code this folder and the prompt in START_HERE_FOR_CLAUDE.md. This package plans the web experience for students, instructors and teaching assistants. It is a specification and reference packet, not an implemented web app.

Prepared 4 November 2026 for the owner and their frontend developer. All sample institutions, people, grades and records are fictional.

What to build

First create an editable, offline HTML/CSS/JavaScript design prototype with coherent sample state and linked pages. Then the frontend developer can refine its appearance and port it to their chosen framework. Do not start backend, native apps, live integrations, deployment, paid AI or authentication services from this handoff.

The proposed catalogue contains 60 required web page templates, including the shared system-state template, plus 3 optional templates. This is a new academic planning inventory. It does not mean 60 completed features, and it does not replace or renumber the historical 50-destination/100-platform atlas. Dialogs, states and role variants are specified inside templates. Some templates can share an implementation component while keeping their distinct URLs and permissions.

“Required” means needed to complete this academic design brief. It is not a claim that all 60 pages belong in a first production release. Follow the staged build sequence and the page priorities.

Reading order

  1. spec/01_PRODUCT_AND_SCOPE.md: purpose, limits, product vocabulary and proposal status.
  2. spec/02_NAVIGATION_AND_PERMISSIONS.md: shells, route conventions and role authority.
  3. spec/03_SHARED_UI_AND_STATES.md: controls, design direction, responsive behavior and recovery.
  4. PAGE_CATALOGUE.md or data/pages.json: every page's fields, actions, validation, states, dialogs and acceptance checks.
  5. spec/04_WORKFLOWS_AND_RECORDS.md, data/fixtures.json and data/mock-service-contracts.json: connected behavior, concrete examples and later service-boundary shapes.
  6. spec/05_BUILD_AND_ACCEPTANCE.md: HTML-first sequence and review checklist.
  7. spec/06_DECISIONS_AND_TRACEABILITY.md: new proposed defaults, open decisions and all coworker feedback.
  8. research/: public evidence, dates and limits. This research supports requirements; it is not user testing or proof of demand.

Source hierarchy

For this new academic brief: owner instructions in the current engagement take priority, then the new specification and decision register, then page data and fixtures. Historical resources are references. Within this package, explicitly named cross-page rules override an accidental inconsistent page example; record and repair the discrepancy instead of inventing behavior. Do not silently resolve an open institutional policy question as a universal rule.

The original Whiteboard work accepted design direction and many workflows. New grading policy, groups, learner grades, TA calendar and other extensions here are proposed defaults for the developer's first HTML, not separately owner-accepted product policies. The owner has authorized this planning and packaging work. They have not approved every new requirement individually or authorized production implementation.

Included resources

  • A complete standalone HTML report, Markdown catalogue and machine-readable page specifications.
  • Fictional fixtures, workflow/journey inventory, permission table, proposed decisions and feedback traceability.
  • Original Whiteboard color/component CSS and selected academic source examples, with provenance.
  • The existing complete prototype as a historical reference. It contains wider campus roles; those are out of scope for the new build. It demonstrates older accepted designs and does not contain the newly specified missing workflows.
  • Local sample handout and submission SVG assets with text alternatives. They are fictional design fixtures.
  • Dependency-free build/verification tools and a SHA-256 inventory for this package.
  • FRONTEND_CHECKLIST.csv for the receiving developer's progress and VERIFICATION.md for the checks and limits of this delivery.

The coworker's original PDF, interview workbook, credentials, browser-local feedback, .git, caches and unrelated project folders are excluded. The feedback is normalized and traced in this packet; no private PDF upload was used for research.

Verify the delivered package

Extract the ZIP first. From the extracted folder, run python tools/verify_handoff.py (or py -3 tools/verify_handoff.py on Windows). It checks hashes, catalogue structure, IDs, source references, local links and fixture arithmetic. No dependencies or network are required. If Node is available, node tools/check_report.cjs exercises the report controller with DOM doubles. python tools/build_handoff.py --refresh-manifest rebuilds the report, catalogue, derived inventories and manifest after intentional edits; run the verifier again. Refreshing the manifest declares a new intended package state; verify the delivered ZIP before making edits.

Source/package checks do not establish browser accessibility or responsive usability. This package was not visually accepted in a browser. Review the future product HTML with the developer in a permitted browser, then record actual results separately from owner design approval.

Resource guide and provenance

Use these files to understand the existing identity and accepted academic concepts. The new W catalogue supplies missing workflows and current academic-only scope. Resources are not an instruction to recreate the broader historical product.

ResourceHow to use it
design-system/tokens.css and components.cssOriginal shared palette, typography, controls and web/iPhone styling. Copy/adapt the web rules into the new design. iPhone-specific rules are references only.

historical-prototype.htmlThe original complete offline click-through prototype. It includes eight roles and campus scope. Review its student/instructor/TA views for visual continuity; do not copy the campus/admin navigation into the new app.
history/decisions.mdHistorical D1-D65, including later acceptance and delegation. Earlier draft comments are retained as history. New WD defaults live in the new decision register.
history/state_checklist.md and history/CONTRACT.mdEarlier state/integrity requirements. Plain-text source paths inside these records refer to the original project.

sample-assets/Newly authored fictional handout, individual/group specimen PDFs, work text and SVG preview; local placeholders with accessible text equivalents. PDF assets are frozen samples, not regenerated by the documentation builder.
provenance.jsonOriginal project path, original SHA-256 and included path for each selected resource, with transformations explicitly recorded.

Selected JS files are a source reading collection, not a standalone runnable build. Their original batch loader/build chain and other domains are intentionally not included. The historical HTML prototype is already self-contained. Create the new prototype from the W specification and fixtures instead of trying to execute a partial historical source collection.

No third-party logos, photographs, commercial icon pack or proprietary software binary is required. The copy contains project-owned reference material and newly authored fictional sample assets; linked vendor/standards documentation remains online with its publisher. This is not a redistribution of third-party help-center pages.

The original coworker PDF/screenshots and interview workbook are not included. Do not infer completed customer discovery from the research packet. No real tool license, customer, uploaded academic record or institutional integration is represented by the fixtures.

Document 28 · Working rules (CLAUDE.md, START_HERE)

The handoff rules file and the start-here guide.

Instructions for the receiving Claude Code session

Read START_HERE_FOR_CLAUDE.md, the scope and permission specifications, and the page catalogue before editing. This folder is a developer handoff for a new academic web prototype. Do not infer production implementation from historical status labels or unrelated campus screens.

Use data/pages.json as the consolidated page catalogue. The two component page JSON files are authoring sources; tools/build_handoff.py merges them and builds the readable report. Edit those source files when updating page specifications. The UI prototype that you create is a separate deliverable: do not overwrite REPORT.html or historical reference HTML.

Treat W01-W60 as proposed web templates and O01-O03 as optional. Keep legacy S/P IDs as crosswalk references, not application routes. An optional assistant/award feature must not become a required menu item or a dependency of a core journey.

Preserve graded versus released, receipt versions, group membership at submission, explicit TA authority, personal calendar privacy, and source ownership. A role picker is a prototype aid, not authentication. Never reveal staff-only fields while rendering a student view. Show simulated saves/delivery/imports as samples. Do not claim localStorage is a secure academic record system.

Use plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript for the first reviewable design. Keep editable files under a separate prototype/ folder, plus an offline bundle if needed. Do not add React/Next, a paid UI service, a backend or a deployment merely to view the design. The frontend developer chooses their eventual stack. Use a deterministic scenario clock and fictional fixtures. Avoid network fonts, CDNs and real school/vendor logins in the offline artifact.

Honor browser/tool restrictions in the receiving environment. If local-file browsing is blocked, do not route around the restriction through localhost or another transport. Ask for permitted user-assisted visual inspection and distinguish that evidence from source checks. Do not claim that every browser/device has passed from one inspected environment.

Build in the stages in spec/05_BUILD_AND_ACCEPTANCE.md. Finish complete journeys with controls that change the displayed sample record. Do not draw 60 disconnected cards and call the app complete. Where a function is deliberately not simulated, provide a clear explanatory state instead of fake success. For each stage, report pages, working transitions, scenario states, checks, limitations and next work in a developer-owned progress log.

Do not automatically commit, publish, message another person or upload the package. Do not copy the owner’s complete source folder to a third-party service. Do not overwrite reference resources. These instructions authorize frontend prototype design within the receiving user's request; production operations require their own scope.

Prompt to give your frontend developer's Claude Code

Copy the text below after extracting this ZIP and opening the extracted folder as the workspace.

> We are designing Whiteboard, an academic web app for students, instructors and teaching assistants. Read CLAUDE.md, README.md, spec/01_PRODUCT_AND_SCOPE.md, spec/02_NAVIGATION_AND_PERMISSIONS.md, spec/03_SHARED_UI_AND_STATES.md, spec/04_WORKFLOWS_AND_RECORDS.md, spec/05_BUILD_AND_ACCEPTANCE.md and spec/06_DECISIONS_AND_TRACEABILITY.md. Then inspect data/pages.json and data/fixtures.json. PAGE_CATALOGUE.md and REPORT.html contain the complete human-readable specifications. Resources are historical visual/source references, not scope expansion. > > Create the first HTML design prototype, with editable local HTML/CSS/JavaScript and an offline bundle, under a new prototype/ directory. Preserve the handoff and reference files. Use the Whiteboard visual identity, coherent course data, student/instructor/TA variants and all relevant recovery states. The frontend developer will refine the visual treatment afterward. Do not choose a production framework or build backend/auth/native services. > > Start by summarizing the academic scope, the proposed page inventory and the critical permission/state rules. Give a short stage plan, then implement Stage 1 from the build guide: the shared shell and the full assignment submission, grading and release journey. Continue through subsequent stages when the user asks, keeping a persistent progress checklist. Read every page specification needed by the current stage, and the connected pages before changing shared behavior. > > Use a visible, separate prototype role/scenario toolbar; never make it look like real product authentication. The actual app navigation must contain only authorized academic destinations. No campus events/clubs/bookings, direct messages or institution administration. Optional achievements and AI remain disabled unless explicitly selected. > > Make the normal and failure-path sample interactions work. Preserve immutable submission/release history and prevent TAs from releasing feedback or changing course policy. Support keyboard use, narrow web layouts, loading/empty/error/offline states and light/dark tokens. Do not treat an HTML phone frame as a native app. Validate in a permitted browser; if unavailable, report the limitation and request user-assisted inspection without bypassing a restriction. Never mark the full product implemented or accessible from source checks alone.

First output expected from Claude

An academic role shell and a navigable course-to-submission-to-feedback prototype, not a marketing landing page and not a redesigned report. The developer should be able to edit the visual CSS without changing course records, grade rules or navigation logic. Save implementation progress against W page IDs. Keep unbuilt pages visible only as clearly labeled prototype coverage entries outside the app shell; do not insert fake functional screens.

Decisions

Whiteboard final design: decisions BD9 onward and C4–C6

BD1–BD8 live in [design/reviews/board-decisions-2026-11-15.md](../reviews/board-decisions-2026-11-15.md) and are not repeated here.

Every entry below was chosen by Claude under owner delegation (CLAUDE.md, 16 Oct 2026) on 15 Nov 2026. They are prototype defaults for the first HTML build, not school-validated policy, and the owner can reverse any of them. Institutional questions stay undecided: first school, late penalties, retention, upload limits and the accessibility support path. Where an entry touches one of them, the prototype shows a labelled sample and decides nothing.

Rules used to choose: the spec or permission matrix beats the drawn screen; take the more conservative authority; invent no institutional policy. Fix ids are rows in tracker/fix_tracker.csv.

C4 · Release recall

  • Question: Does a release have a "recall" that hides results again? (02 #3 (../../research/ux/02_instructors.md))
  • Decision: No recall. The W53 release dialog says: "Students keep this result. You can correct it later. The correction is logged and students see 'Feedback updated'."
  • Why: Final plan line 115. A recall would make "Released" untrustworthy for students; logged correction (synthesis rule 4, Q01.3, D27) already meets the instructor's need to fix mistakes.
  • Affected: C4; journey walk J03, J05, J06 (see design/reviews/journey-walk-2026-11.md).
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

C5 · Anonymous grading

  • Question: How does anonymous grading (03 #5 (../../research/ux/03_tas_grading.md)) fit section-scoped TAs and regrades?
  • Decision: An optional "Hide learner names while grading" setting per assessment. Default off; locked after the first receipt. Graders see stable aliases in random order. Names return at release. Regrades (W54) are always named.
  • Adjusted by the walk (clarified, not reversed): while names are hidden, aliases replace names together on W48, W49, W50 and W51, in file names and routes (the drawn grader shows "aisha-ps4-sample.pdf" and "/grading/ps4/aisha"), and on group receipts; TA allocation views use aliases. Evidence: design/reviews/board-deep-dive-2026-11-15.md:1764, :1751.
  • Why: Final plan line 116. Hiding names is compatible with TA scoping because the allocation still limits which receipts a TA sees; the reveal point is fixed at release so regrades, which need a released snapshot (BD24), are never anonymous.
  • Affected: C5; journey walk J03, J08.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

C6 · Student label for graded, not released work

  • Question: What does a student see after grading but before release? (01 #11 (../../research/ux/01_students.md) suggests "Being reviewed".)
  • Decision: No change at grading. The student sees "Received · Feedback not released yet" until release.
  • Why: Final plan line 117. Any student-visible change at grading leaks that grading happened (synthesis C6); BD9 makes "Received" the status word.
  • Affected: C6; journey walk J02, J03, J06.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD9 · Status word for handed-in work

  • Question: "Submitted" (synthesis rule 1) or "Received"?
  • Decision: "Received" is the status and "Submit" is the verb. The synthesis's "Submitted" is replaced in the status vocabulary.
  • Why: Final plan line 118. "Received" states what the system did (the receipt), not what the student attempted.
  • Affected: DD-1.13.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD10 · Native presentation

  • Question: Are iPhone and iPad drawn as native apps or as narrow web?
  • Decision: iPhone and iPad are drawn as planned native apps ("planned presentation"); narrow web follows BD1.
  • Why: Final plan line 119 and owner answer 1 (plan §6). Native parity is planned, not implemented.
  • Affected: DD-1.03, DD-2.14, DD-3.20, DD-4.15.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD11 · Platform tier rule

  • Question: Which tier (full, review and protect, handoff) does each page get on each platform?
  • Decision: Applied in order: T1 web is always full. T2 a page whose board roles contain s or g is full on iPad and iPhone. T3 W42, W60 and O02 are handoff on iPad and iPhone. T4 on iPad, W48, W49, W51 (single-learner view), W53 (review only) and W57 are full. T5 every other staff-only page is review and protect, with the Part 5 protective-action text as its note. BD6 wins over the Part 5 device table and fix 5.18: their iPad editing requests are kept as notes only and never change the tier.
  • Why: Fully determined by the board PAGES roles plus BD6; gives web 63/0/0, iPad 41/19/3, iPhone 36/24/3 (final plan lines 70–74).
  • Affected: DD-5.18, tracker/page_tracker.csv.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD12 · Wrong-account invitation details

  • Question: What does W03 show when an invitation is opened in the wrong account?
  • Decision: Mask the wrong-account details on W03 (partial address; no course or role).
  • Why: Final plan table (1.02); the W03 spec's acceptance check asks for masking.
  • Affected: DD-1.02.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD13 · Email delivery defaults

  • Question: W04, W10 and the W08 fixture disagree on email delivery.
  • Decision: Receipts are always emailed; all other email is off by default.
  • Why: Final plan table (1.15); keeps the receipt promise (synthesis rule 2) and the few-alerts rule (rule 7).
  • Affected: DD-1.15.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD14 · Cancelling registrar classes

  • Question: May an instructor cancel a registrar-sourced class on W32?
  • Decision: Registrar classes get a "Class notice" instead; Cancel exists only for Whiteboard-owned events.
  • Why: Final plan table (2.01); registrar meetings are read-only (WD15, Spec 01).
  • Affected: DD-2.01.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD15 · Module completion

  • Question: Does module completion require finishing an assessment (W16)?
  • Decision: Module completion stays separate from submission.
  • Why: Final plan table (2.08); the spec keeps module state separate.
  • Affected: DD-2.08.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD16 · Grading-deadline authority

  • Question: W07 says instructor-only, W32 says instructor or TA.
  • Decision: The instructor sets grading deadlines; TAs see them read-only.
  • Why: Final plan table (2.11, 6.16); the more conservative authority.
  • Affected: DD-2.11, DD-6.16.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD17 · W21 confirmation

  • Question: Does W21 confirm the exact payload or show an integrity attestation?
  • Decision: W21 confirms the exact payload (items, files and what will be sent, with blanks flagged); any attestation sits inside the same submit dialog, not in place of the payload.
  • Why: Final plan table (3.04); the spec checks the exact payload and synthesis rule 2 needs a review step.
  • Affected: DD-3.04.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD18 · When the course total moves

  • Question: Does the course total move with the item release or with its own projection release?
  • Decision: The total moves with the item release, and the W53 preview shows the change (84.50% → 85.17%).
  • Why: Final plan table (3.09); matches the W23 banner and keeps one release step.
  • Affected: DD-3.09.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD19 · Letter grade source

  • Question: Where do letter grades and rounding come from?
  • Decision: The letter grade comes only from the W52 policy; no screen shows a letter that W52 does not define.
  • Why: Final plan table (3.10). Boundaries and rounding are a course policy set in W52; the sample values are labelled fictional.
  • Affected: DD-3.10.

BD24 · Regrade fixture

  • Question: W54 shows a regrade request on a held, unreleased PS4.

BD25 · No scores in previews

  • Question: W05 Home and W08 Activity show "8 / 10" and "8 of 10" for Quiz 2.
  • Decision: Preview cards and activity items carry no score or grade on any platform. They say "Feedback ready" and link to W23 or W27, where the released result is shown.
  • Why: The W08 spec, C14 and WD19 say previews carry no score (DD-1.01); the spec beats the drawn screen.
  • Affected: DD-1.01, DD-2.02.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD26 · TA navigation and page access follow the permission matrix

  • Question: The TA shell shows full instructor navigation (W14), and the W42/W59 TA states differ from no_access_default.
  • Decision: Staff navigation is filtered by the Spec 02 permission matrix: a TA sees only allowed entries and informative read-only views. A page whose matrix entry is no_access_default for TAs (W42, W59) shows the standard W13 "not available to your account" state. Instructor navigation includes Assessments and Syllabus, and the W18 staff breadcrumb names the course, not "Builder".
  • Why: Spec 02 (spec/docs/04-spec-02-navigation-and-permissions.html): "A TA sees only allowed entries and informative read-only views." The matrix beats the drawn screen and is the more conservative authority.
  • Matrix detail (inspection round 1): NAV (spec/docs/19-navigation-map-navigation-json.html) keeps four staff entries for a TA in a scoped mode: Builder W35 read_only, Gradebook W51 assigned_only, People W45 restricted_read_only, Settings W36 read_only. They stay in TA navigation and open labelled read-only or scoped views with no edit affordances. The deep dive's claim that a TA "must not see" them (DD line 619) is rejected against the matrix.
  • Affected: DD-2.03, DD-5.06; journey walk JW-028.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD27 · Quiz score selection

  • Question: W25 and W27 do not show which attempt counts when more than one is allowed.
  • Decision: W25 shows the quiz's attempt count and selection rule before Start, exactly as set in W41 (spec default: 1 attempt; latest completed attempt). W27 names the attempt that counts. The fixture value is labelled sample data.
  • Why: The W41 spec field "Attempts and selection" says "choose highest/latest completed attempt and disclose before start"; synthesis rule 6 asks for the rules before Start.
  • Affected: DD-3.16.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD28 · Individual overrides in group work

  • Question: W47's acceptance check on individual overrides has no UI on that page.
  • Decision: An individual override is made in W49 on one member, with a reason, and never changes the shared group receipt. W47 shows a read-only overrides summary (learner, reason, set by, link to W49). No staff version of W34 is added (BD8).
  • Why: The W47 spec acceptance check ("Individual grade overrides attach to a member with reason and never mutate the shared submitted artifact") and the W49 score panel's "manual override reason" field. Keeps W33/W34 student-only per BD8.
  • Affected: DD-4.08.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD29 · Discussion fixture

  • Question: W30 and W31 disagree on the author and reply count of "Projectile motion".
  • Decision: One reconstructed discussion fixture drives both pages. The thread's opening post is the one W31 draws (Aisha), and W30 shows that author and the fixture's real reply count.
  • Why: The fixtures panel lists people but no discussion record, so the fixture is reconstructed and labelled as such (final plan §6, owner answer 2). The detail page shows the post itself, so it is the more specific source.
  • Affected: DD-4.11.
  • chosen by Claude under owner delegation.

BD30 · Page priorities

  • Question: W28/W30 are "core" in their specs and "optional" in matrix.txt; W56 is "follow-on" but W30 depends on it.
  • Decision: The priority written in each page spec is canonical: W28 and W30 are core, W56 stays follow-on. In the prototype W30's discussions come from fixtures, so W30 does not need W56 to be built; W30's staff "Set up discussion" control links to W56.
  • Why: The deep dive's corrections note (line 21) says the matrix column came from a faulty script and to use the page spec's priority.
  • Affected: DD-4.16.
